default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vi: Whenever I look at this photo, I always remember that person.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative directly modifies the noun 「写真」 that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle 「を」 marks the object affected by the action of looking at 「見る」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern 「V-る ＋ と」 connects sentences with the meaning of a necessary condition: whenever the earlier action occurs, the later reaction or result follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb of frequent occurrence that modifies the predicate 「思い出す」 at the end of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The demonstrative modifies the noun 「人」 and refers to a person who is far away or to something both people know about.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle 「の」 connects to and expresses possession for the noun 「こと」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: The phrase 「〜のことを」 combines with the particle 「を」 to show the object of one's thoughts and nostalgic feelings.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: The main predicate verb of the sentence, expressing the natural reaction of remembering when the condition in the first clause occurs.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.why: This sentence describes a habit or a natural, necessary reaction: whenever the condition of looking at the photo occurs, feelings of remembering that person automatically arise. Therefore, the conjunction pattern 「〜と」 combined with the adverb 「いつも」 is the most suitable.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It has the meaning of remembering after looking at something at a specific time, with less emphasis on a natural regular pattern. The expression is 「〜と」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It is used to give advice or receive information from another person, not for an event that naturally and inevitably happens to the speaker.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.tip: When they want to say that they remember someone together with all the memories, Japanese people usually use 「人のことを思い出す」 instead of using only 「人を見る」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ と
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vi: I go to the convenience store about three times a week.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle 「に」 follows a time unit and shows the reference point or cycle used to count frequency.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The number with the counter 「回」 and the degree particle 「くらい」 modifies the frequency of going.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle 「に」 shows the destination of the movement verb 「行きます」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The main predicate is in the polite form ます and describes a repeated action as a habit.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.cn: Time period ＋ に ＋ Number of times ＋ V
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.why: This is the standard structure for expressing frequency in Japanese: the particle 「に」 follows a time unit that serves as the cycle reference, such as a week. It is followed by the number of times and a movement verb toward the destination 「コンビニに」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It does not express a regular frequency for each time unit. Instead, it means the total time allowed to complete something within one week.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often forget the particle 「に」 after the time period when expressing frequency. They mistakenly say 「1週間 3回」 instead of 「週に3回」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vi: I will say it only once, so please listen very carefully.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle 「だけ」 follows the counter 「一度」 and expresses a unique limitation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The conjunction 「から」 connects a clause expressing a reason based on the speaker's intention and personal judgment.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The adverb 「よく」 comes before a verb and modifies the manner of performing an action carefully and attentively.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The gentle command pattern 「V-ます ＋ なさい」 is used when a superior, parent, or teacher asks someone of lower status to perform an action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.cn: V-ます (remove ます) ＋ なさい
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.why: The first clause gives a reason and a limitation using 「〜から」 combined with 「だけ」. In the second clause, the speaker, being in a superior position, uses the instructive command pattern 「〜なさい」 to ask the listener to listen carefully.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: This is a normal polite request between equals. It does not have the instructive tone of a superior like 「〜なさい」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses a prohibition, meaning that someone must not do something. This is the opposite of the required action expressed by 「〜なさい」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q3.kobun.tip: The pattern 「〜なさい」 is used only when a superior speaks to someone of lower status, or when parents tell their children what to do. It must not be used with equals or superiors.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vi: If I do not wear glasses, I cannot see the writing on the blackboard clearly.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle 「は」 makes the pronoun 「わたし」 the main topic of the whole sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle 「を」 marks the object affected by the action of putting on 「かける」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.2.vi: if I do not wear them
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The negative conditional pattern 「V-ない ＋ と」 means that if this action is not done, an unfavorable result will inevitably follow in the next clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle 「の」 modifies the location of the following noun 「字」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle 「が」 combines with the natural-ability verb 「見えません」 to show the object received by the eyes.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: The natural-ability intransitive verb 「見える」 is in the polite negative form. It means that the eyes normally cannot receive the image by themselves.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.why: The pattern 「〜ないと」 gives an essential condition. Combined with the natural perception verb 「見えない」, it describes a limitation in eyesight when glasses are not available.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It only means that someone has no chance to watch something or is forbidden to watch it because of external circumstances, while 「見えません」 refers to the eyes' natural visual ability.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It has the same conditional meaning, but 「〜ないと」 is more conversational and emphasizes the obvious inevitable result more strongly.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q4.kobun.tip: Clearly distinguish 「見えない」, meaning that the eyes naturally cannot see clearly because of poor eyesight, from 「見られない」, meaning that someone cannot watch because of circumstances such as having no ticket or being forbidden to watch.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vi: Hana, could you please listen to my story for a moment?
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: A form of address used to call someone's name and attract their attention before making a request.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle 「の」 shows possession and modifies the following noun 「話」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle 「を」 marks the object received by the action of listening 「聞く」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.3.vi: could you please listen to me
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The formal request pattern 「V-て ＋ いただけませんか」 politely and modestly asks the other person to perform an action to help the speaker.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.why: To make a tactful request, the speaker combines the verb in the て form with the negative potential form of humble language, 「いただく」, to create a polite request.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: This is a direct request and sounds more demanding and less formal than 「〜ていただけませんか」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: This is an informal request pattern for friends and close people. It is not formal and does not show the same respect as 「〜ていただけませんか」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.tip: The pattern 「〜ていただけませんか」 means asking ANOTHER PERSON to do something for the speaker. Do not confuse it with asking permission for ONESELF to do 「〜てもいいですか」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q5.kobun.cn: Vて形 ＋ いただけませんか
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vi: If you plan to go to the dentist, you should brush your teeth before you go.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle 「に」 indicates the object or destination of the action of going to the dentist.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern 「V-る ＋ なら」 receives a topic or intention to do something in the future and is used to give suitable advice.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle 「を」 marks the object affected by the action of brushing 「磨く」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern 「V-て ＋ から」 expresses a time sequence: the action of brushing must be completed before the next action is done.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern 「V-た ＋ ほうがいい」 is used to give advice or suggest a better course of action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The predicate adjective ends the advice sentence and confirms that the suggested action is the best choice.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.why: The first clause uses 「〜なら」 to receive the listener's intention to go to the dentist. The second clause combines the sequence connector 「〜てから」 with the advice structure 「〜たほうがいい」 to show the preparation needed before going.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: 「〜たら」 requires the action of going to the dentist to happen first, with the second clause happening afterward. Therefore, it cannot be used to advise someone to prepare BEFORE going.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: Using the dictionary form expresses less of a specific best-choice recommendation than using the past form 「〜たほうがいい」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.tip: When advising someone to prepare before a trip or event, you must use 「〜なら」, not 「〜たら」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・N ＋ なら / Vた形 ＋ ほうがいい
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vi: It is winter, but it is warm, isn't it?
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun 冬 combines with なのに to describe something unexpectedly opposite to the natural expectation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in い acts as the predicate describing the weather.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: A polite sentence ending combined with the particle ね to seek agreement from the listener.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.why: The pattern 「〜のに」 shows something happening contrary to expectations or common sense, with a feeling of surprise. When it connects to a noun 「冬」, grammar requires adding 「な」 to form 「冬なのに」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It is used for the assumption "even if ... still ...", while 「のに」 emphasizes an actual situation together with surprise or dissatisfaction.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: It only connects two contrasting clauses objectively and gently. It does not express the surprise shown by 「のに」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to add 「な」 when connecting a noun or an adjective ending in な with 「のに」. They may incorrectly write 「冬のに」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな（な）・Nな ＋ のに
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vi: Hana has just come back. It was only about five minutes ago.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: Makes Hana the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: A time adverb for the recent past, stressing that an event has just happened.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: A verb in the た form directly modifies the formal noun ところ.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: A sentence pattern showing that an action was completed only a few minutes ago.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: A quantity phrase with くらい showing an estimated period of time.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: A predicate confirming a point in time, with the particle よ to provide information to the listener.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.why: The pattern「Vた＋ところだ」 describes an action that has just ended. The sentence includes the adverb「さっき」(a moment ago), and the following phrase explains「five minutes ago」, further confirming that the action was completed in the recent past.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: It also means "just," but it depends on the speaker's subjective feeling, so it can be used for an event that happened a few weeks or even a few months ago.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: Describes an action happening at the moment of speaking ("is on the way back"), rather than an action that has already finished.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.tip: Clearly distinguish「Vたところ」(has just finished doing something) from「Vるところ」(is about to do something).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q8.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ ところだ / ところです
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vi: Although I asked him many times, he still did not help me.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb of frequency stressing that the request was made many times.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The dependent conjunction "〜のに" links clauses showing contrast, together with feelings of dissatisfaction and disappointment.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle "は" makes the subject of the following clause the topic of discussion.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb is changed to the "〜てくれる" form in the past negative, describing the other person's failure to do something helpful for me.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.why: The structure '〜のに' is chosen because the result in the following clause (not helping) is contrary to the usual expectation after asking many times. It also shows the speaker's regret and dissatisfaction.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 'お願いしても' is used, it only expresses a purely conditional concessive relationship. It does not contain the clear dissatisfaction or reproach expressed by 'のに'.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If '手伝ってもらえなかった' is used, the sentence is viewed from the speaker's perspective (I did not receive help), while '手伝ってくれなかった' emphasizes the other person's action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.tip: The clause after '〜のに' must describe an event that happened or an objective fact. It must never be followed by structures showing commands, intention, or invitations, such as 〜てください and 〜ましょう.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな＋な・N＋な ＋ のに
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vi: This work must be completed today.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A demonstrative that directly modifies the noun "仕事" that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle "は" makes the work the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The suffix "〜中" combined with the particle "に" indicates the deadline by which the action must be completed.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The causative/transitive verb "終わらせる" is changed to the "〜なければならない" form to show a compulsory duty.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.why: The work 'この仕事' has '今日中に' as its deadline. The transitive/causative form '終わらせる' with the obligation pattern '〜なければならない' shows the responsibility to actively finish the work.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If the intransitive verb '終わらなければならない' is used, the sentence means that the work ends by itself. It does not clearly show the worker's intention and effort as '終わらせなければならない' does.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced with '終わらせなくてもいい', the sentence changes completely to mean permission. Completion is not required.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.tip: Distinguish '〜中に (〜じゅうに)', which means a deadline (it must be finished before the day ends), from '〜中 (〜じゅう)', which means carrying out the action throughout that period.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q2.kobun.cn: Vない形（〜ない → 〜なければならない）
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vi: I have no money, and I have no job either. What should I do from now on?
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle "も" combines with the conjunction "し" to list the first reason in a series of difficult circumstances.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle "も" adds a second item that shares the same state of not existing.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The ending "〜んです" explains the difficult situation and prepares for the question that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: A time adverb marking the period beginning at the present and continuing into the future.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The question word "どう" combines with the conditional verb form "〜ば" to state the situation that needs to be solved.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: An adjective combined with a question particle forms a complete sentence asking for advice.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.why: The pattern '〜し' combines with the particle 'も' to build up several negative reasons and explain the difficult situation. It then uses '〜ばいいですか' to ask the listener for an opinion or advice.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 'お金も仕事もないから' is used, it only explains one simple cause. It does not list several factors in a cumulative way like '〜し'.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: The pattern '〜たらいいですか' is equivalent in meaning to '〜ばいいですか' when asking for advice, but it sounds slightly more natural and common in conversation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.tip: When listing several reasons with '〜し', the factors should point in the same direction (all positive or all negative). The particles 'が/は' should be replaced with 'も' to make the list more connected.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな（だ/な）・N（だ） ＋ し ｜ Vば ＋ いいですか
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vi: There is too much luggage, so it does not seem possible to fit it into this bag.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the state adjective 多くて.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in い changes to the て form to connect sentences and show the reason leading to the following clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: A demonstrative directly modifies the noun かばん that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates the place or destination receiving the action of putting something in.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb in the ます form, with ます removed, combines with そうもない to strongly judge that fitting is unlikely.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.cn: Vます（without ます） ＋ そうもない / そうにない
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.why: The first clause uses the adjective in the て form (多くて) to state an objective cause. The second clause uses 入りそうもない to express a direct judgment that the event is almost impossible.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: A similar meaning, but with slightly weaker negation than そうもない.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: A normal negative prediction form (ない changes to なさそうだ), without the strong emphasis on improbability found in そうもない.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q4.kobun.tip: Remember that a verb combined with そうもない must be in the ます form with ます removed. Do not use the dictionary form or the past form.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q4.tokens.6.m: is unlikely to, does not seem to
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vi: Because I played video games every day, my eyesight has become worse.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: A time-frequency adverb modifying the action of playing games.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern ため follows a verb in the past form and shows an objective cause leading to a negative result in the following clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject of the change of state in the following clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending in い changes to the くなって form and combines with てしまう to express an unwanted worsening of the situation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.why: The structure ため（に） describes an objective cause-and-effect relationship, often leading to an unwanted result. The following clause uses てしまった to stress regret about the worsening of eyesight.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It is more conversational and shows the speaker's subjectivity more than ため, which is objective and formal.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It gives a reason in a gentle, polite, narrative way and places less stress on necessary cause and effect than ため.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.tip: To avoid confusion about how to connect the parts: a noun before ため must have の (Nの ため), while an adjective before な must keep な (Aな ため).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな（な）・N（の） ＋ ため（に）
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vi: When I went to that delicious cake shop, the customers were all women.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の replaces が as the subject in the relative clause modifying 店.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in い combines with ケーキの to form a clause that directly modifies the noun 店.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the destination of the movement action 行ったら.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb in the たら form describes discovering an actual situation after carrying out an action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle は makes お客 the topic to be explained by the predicate.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle ばかり attaches after a noun to show that the object is mostly or almost entirely made up of that group.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.why: The first clause uses Vたら to show that the speaker discovered the actual situation after arriving at the shop. The second clause uses ばかり after the noun 女の人 to emphasize the overall impression that all or most of the customers were women.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: だけ shows an absolute limit (100%, with no one else), while ばかり emphasizes an overwhelming impression and a dominant number.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: しか…ない carries a feeling of regret or denial that there was no one else besides that group.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.tip: Do not mistake the particle の in 'ケーキの おいしい' for possession; here, the particle の replaces が in a relative clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q6.kobun.cn: N ＋ ばかり / Vて ＋ ばかり
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vi: I thought the soccer match would be canceled, but surprisingly, it was decided that it would take place.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の modifies the noun 試合 to identify the sport.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は introduces the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に combines with the verb なる to show the resulting state of being postponed or canceled.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle と quotes the content of a thought before the verb 思ってたら.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The ていたら form of the verb (shortened as てたら) expresses an earlier thought, followed by an opposite real result.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.5.vi: it was decided that it would take place
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern ことになる expresses something decided by circumstances or the organizers.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.why: The first clause uses 思ってたら to express the speaker's initial personal thought. The second clause uses ことになった to show that the event happened according to the organizers' decision, beyond the individual's control.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: ことにする shows an active decision made by the speaker, rather than a decision caused by circumstances or other people.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: ことになっている shows a rule, schedule, or custom that has been set and remains in effect.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.tip: Do not confuse ことにする (the person decides for themselves) with ことになる (the decision is made by circumstances or an organization).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q7.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない ＋ ことになる / ことになった
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vi: I may be late tomorrow because of work, so please go ahead without me.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は introduces the speaker as the topic.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: This time expression acts as an adverb and identifies when the action of being late will happen.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle で shows the cause or reason why the speaker may be late.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The speculation pattern かもしれない combines with the particle から to give the reason for the prediction and support the request that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: This adverb shows priority and modifies the following verb.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb is changed to the てください form to make a polite suggestion or request.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな（drop だ）・N（drop だ） ＋ かもしれない
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.why: The first clause presents a low-certainty possibility (about 50%) using かもしれない together with から as the basis for the request てください in the second clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: はずだ shows near-100% certainty based on clear evidence, so it does not fit a modest prediction about the speaker's own schedule.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: 〜そうだ shows a direct prediction based on signs visible now that something is about to happen.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q8.kobun.tip: When combined with a noun or an adjective ending in な, だ must be omitted before かもしれない (for example, 雨かもしれない, not 雨だかもしれない).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vi: I watch five movies a month.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.sk: Period of time に ＋ 数量 ＋ N を ＋ Vます
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に attaches after a time period to set the reference point for how often an action is performed.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: This counter phrase modifies the number of times the action is performed.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the action of watching.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The main verb is conjugated in the polite ます form.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.cn: Period of time ＋ に ＋ 数量 (Shows how often an action is performed within a unit of time)
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.why: The particle に attaches after a time period (１か月) and sets the regular time unit. The counter phrase (５本) comes before the object or verb to show how many times the action is performed during that time unit.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: で shows the total time allowed to finish something (watching five movies within one month), while に shows a regular frequency.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: Without に, the sentence sounds more like a raw list of numbers than a precise regular-frequency structure.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t10-q9.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly use the particle で instead of に to express regular frequency (use '１か月に５本', not '１か月で５本' to mean five movies a month).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vi: I had done my homework, but the teacher did not come.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the direct object of doing the homework.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.1.vi: even though I had done it
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern のに connects two clauses whose actual results are opposite to expectations.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject performing the action in the following clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb is in the negative past form and serves as the main predicate that ends the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.why: The sentence uses のに to connect two contrasting clauses. It shows regret and dissatisfaction because the second event (the teacher did not come) went against the preparation in the first clause (the homework had been done).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It states a hypothetical or obvious concessive condition and does not contain the disappointment or blame expressed by のに.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It simply connects two clauses that contrast in information, without the regret and surprise felt by the speaker.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.tip: Before のに, nouns and adjectives ending in な must change to the な ending form (such as 雨なのに and 暇なのに); だ cannot be used.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな(な)・Nな ＋ のに
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.vi: There has been a car parked in front of my house for three days, and it has stayed exactly as it was.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects nouns and locates the noun 前 in space.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the place where the car is parked.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.2.n: This noun phrase shows the continuous length of time that the state has lasted.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the subject of the parking situation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.4.vi: is still parked exactly as it was.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern Vた ＋ まま describes a state that remains unchanged after the action has happened.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.why: The pattern 〜まま combines with the past-tense verb 止まった to emphasize that the car has been left exactly as it was after being parked, without moving, for three days.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 止まりっぱなし carries a clearer sense of criticism about carelessness or neglect than 止まったまま.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.tip: With verbs, this structure uses Vた＋まま (doing something and leaving it that way) or Vない＋まま (not doing something and leaving it that way). It cannot be combined directly with the dictionary form Vる.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q10.kobun.cn: Vた・Vない・Nの・Aい・Aな ＋ まま
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.vi: It is already 11 o'clock. You have school tomorrow too, so children, go to bed early.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.0.n: This independent predicate clause states the current time.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle も is added to the time noun to emphasize that the event continues as usual.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern なんだから gives an obvious reason as a strong basis for the command.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は identifies the people affected by the command.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.4.n: This adverb is formed from the adjective 早く and modifies the following command verb.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.ch.5.n: The predicate is the direct imperative form (命令形) of the verb 寝る.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.cn: V/A/N普通形 (N/Aな＋な) ＋ のだから・んだから / Group 2 verbs: drop る ＋ ろ
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.why: The first clause uses the structure なんだから to give an obvious reason and create a basis that requires the listener to perform the firm command ねろ in the second clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.vs.0.d: Using 早く寝なさい sounds more caring, like a parent advising a child, while the direct imperative form ねろ sounds like harsh scolding or a very strong order.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q11.kobun.tip: The direct imperative form (命令形, such as ねろ) is extremely forceful and must never be used with superiors or people outside the family.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.vi: According to the letter, Tanaka is still said to be well.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.0.n: The pattern N によると comes at the beginning of a sentence to cite the source of the information received.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the person mentioned in the source of the information.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.2.vi: is said to still be well.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.ch.2.n: The hearsay pattern 〜そうです follows the plain form (Aな＋だ) to report information that was heard or read.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.why: The information-source structure N によると must always match the reporting ending 〜そうだ / 〜そうです at the end of the main clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.vs.0.d: If だ is changed to 元気そうです, it becomes a pattern for judging from appearance (“looks healthy”), which conflicts with receiving indirect information from 手紙によると.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.tip: When used with the information source によると, the sentence ending must be the reporting form (with an adjective ending in な, keep だ unchanged: 元気だそうだ), to avoid mistakenly changing だ into the visual-judgment form.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q12.kobun.cn: N ＋ によると / V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ そうだ（伝聞）
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.kobun.vi: I’m sorry, but if anything happens to my father, could you please call me? I will come right away.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.0.n: It serves as a polite opening before making a request.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks the person affected by or involved in an event.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.2.n: The question word combines with か to form an indefinite word that serves as the subject of the verb ある.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb ある is changed to the たら form to express a hypothetical future condition.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the calling action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern 〜てくださいませんか is used to make a polite and formal request.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.6.n: The adverb modifies the verb 来ます and shows the speed and timing of the action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.7.vi: because I will come right away.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.kobun.ch.7.n: The verb 来る in the polite form is used with the linking particle ので to explain the reason for the previous request.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.kobun.why: The sentence uses the hypothetical structure 〜たら to set a condition, combines it with the formal request pattern 〜てくださいませんか to ask the other person to call, and ends with 〜ので to add a reasonable explanation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.kobun.vs.0.d: It has a direct request tone and is less polite and less formal than 〜てくださいませんか.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.kobun.vs.1.d: It is still a request in question form, but it is more casual and is usually used with friends or equals.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the politeness levels of 〜てくださいませんか (very polite and formal) and 〜てくれませんか (more casual).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.tokens.5.m: if there is / if something happens
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q13.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くださいませんか
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vi: My child refuses to study and does nothing but play all day.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: It modifies the noun 子ども to identify someone or something belonging to the speaker’s family.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the noun the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is changed to the ないで form to show that the action of studying is not done before another action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb is changed to the て form to connect directly to the following grammar pattern.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern 〜てばかりいる describes an action repeated many times and includes a complaining attitude.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.why: The sentence combines the structure Vないで to show that the child skips studying, with てばかりいる at the end to emphasize that the playing continues constantly and annoys the speaker.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It only limits quantity or range and does not show criticism or complaint like ばかり.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It simply describes an action happening at the time of speaking or a normal habit, without a negative tone.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.tip: Clearly distinguish Vないで (do B without doing A) from Vなくて (only the cause or reason leading to the following clause).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q2.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ ばかりいる / N ＋ ばかり
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vi: Yamada is also tall, but he is not as tall as Tanaka.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle も replaces は to introduce a topic with the same meaning of height.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が accompanies a body part to describe the subject’s attribute.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が connects two clauses that contrast in degree.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle ほど sets the comparison standard and is used with the negative predicate that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective ending in い is changed to the negative form and serves as the predicate in the unequal comparison clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.why: The first clause uses が to acknowledge a feature of the first person, while the second uses N＋ほど＋the negative form to clearly show a lower degree than the comparison standard.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses a higher comparison (田中さんより高い - taller than Tanaka) and has the opposite meaning from the unequal comparison structure ほど〜ない.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It is mainly used to estimate an equal or approximate degree and is less common in an absolute negative comparison pattern such as ほど.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.tip: In the pattern Nほど, the following clause must be in the negative form to mean “not as ... as N.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q3.kobun.cn: N ＋ ほど ＋ Vない・Aくない・Aではない
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vi: If I received ten million yen, I would like to travel to many countries.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb at the beginning of a sentence that signals a supposition.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: A noun phrase showing the amount of money received in the hypothetical situation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is changed to the たら form and combined with the adverb もし to create a hypothetical conditional clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は marks the person who has the wish in the following clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective ending in な directly modifies the noun 国 that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle を shows the area where the act of traveling takes place.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: The verb ending in たい serves as the main predicate and expresses the speaker’s wish.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.why: The sentence begins with the adverb もし and the verb in the たら form to set up an unreal present assumption, then expresses a personal wish in the following clause with the ending たい.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It is used only for necessary, natural conditions or habits and must never be used with a clause expressing intention or desire (たい) in the following part.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It is usually used to receive information from the other person and then give advice or an evaluation, rather than to make a pure supposition about a situation like たら.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.tip: When the following clause expresses intention or desire, such as 〜たい or 〜つもり, you must use たら, not the condition forms と or ば.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q4.kobun.cn: Vた・Aかった・Aだった・Nだった ＋ ら
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vi: Because the roads are crowded on Sunday, I decided to go on Monday.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes a time reference the topic in order to state an observation about its condition.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the subject of the crowded condition.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The conjunction ので gives an objective reason and makes the statement polite and gentle.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に marks the specific time chosen for carrying out the action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the formal noun こと that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern ことにする expresses a decision personally made by the speaker.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.why: The first clause uses ので to give an objective reason about traffic conditions. This becomes the basis for the speaker’s active decision in the second clause, using the pattern Vる＋ことにした.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It describes something decided because of objective circumstances, rules, or arrangements made by other people, rather than by the speaker personally.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It only expresses an intention or passing thought and has not become a definite decision like ことにした.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.tip: Clearly distinguish ことにする (a decision made by oneself) from ことになる (a decision made by a group or caused by circumstances).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 ＋ ことにする
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vi: Today I went out without eating anything.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes today’s time point the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The question word 何 combines with も and a negative predicate to express complete negation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb takes the ないで form to express a state that accompanies the main action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The main verb is in the polite past form and describes a completed action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.why: The sentence uses the total-negative adverb 何も with the ないで form to describe an accompanying state (being hungry and not having eaten) while carrying out the movement action 出かけました.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It is used to show a cause or reason (because I did not eat, I was hungry), not an accompanying state such as ないで.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: It has a meaning equivalent to ないで, but it is more formal and is often used in writing.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q6.kobun.tip: To express “doing action B in a state of not doing action A,” you must use Vないで, and you must not use Vなくて.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.vi: A: 「Does Mr. Tanaka have a girlfriend yet?」 B: 「No. Since he broke up with his former girlfriend, he has not liked anyone anymore.」
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic of the question.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が used with the verb います marks the object possessed or existing.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: An interrogative predicate with the sentence-ending particle か.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: A negative interjection that opens the answer.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle は repeats the topic, the person being discussed.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle の links nouns and modifies “former girlfriend.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle と marks the person who participated in the breakup.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.7.n: The pattern Vてから marks the starting point of a continuously lasting state.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.8.n: The particle を marks the object toward which the feeling of liking in the phrase 人を好きになる is directed.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.ch.9.n: The i-adjective ending な combines with になる and changes into the past negative form なくなりました to show a change of state.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.why: The sentence uses 〜てから to set the time of the breakup. From that point, the speaker’s mental state continued to change, shown by changing 好きになる into the negative-change form 〜ならなくなる.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 別れたあとで is used, it simply tells the order of two events. It does not emphasize a continuously changing state lasting from that point until now, as 〜てから does.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.tip: Do not confuse 好きにならなくなる (a change of state: no longer liking someone) with 好きじゃない (a static state: not liking someone).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q7.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ から / Aな語幹 ＋ にならなくなる
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vi: That ring was shining like a star.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: A demonstrative that directly modifies the noun 指輪 that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the ring as the topic being described.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern N のように makes a comparison and functions as an adverb modifying the verb.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: A predicate describing a continuing past state in the Vていた form.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.why: The phrase 星のように functions as a comparative adverb before the verb. It directly modifies ひかっていた to describe the way the light shone.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If 星のような is used, it must be followed by a noun, such as 星のような輝き. To modify a verb, you must use 星のように.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the endings 〜のような (used before nouns) and 〜のように (used before verbs or adjectives).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q8.kobun.cn: Nの・V普通形・Aい・Aな ＋ ように
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vi: I worked for only three hours and received as much as 10,000 yen.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle だけ expresses a small limited amount.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を identifies the object affected by the action of working.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The conditional form 〜たら shows that the action was completed and led to the surprising result that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle も follows a number to emphasize that the amount is much larger than expected.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb もらう is in the past potential form and shows the good result achieved.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.why: The sentence clearly contrasts the small condition required (３時間だけ) with the large amount of money received, emphasized by も (１０,０００円も).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If １０,０００円はもらえた is used, the sentence means “received at least 10,000 yen,” and loses the surprise that the amount is very large, expressed by も.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t11-q9.kobun.tip: After a quantity, the particle も emphasizes a surprisingly large amount (translated as “as many as/as much as”), not the meaning “also.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.vi: Shun came to school without doing his homework.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern Vないで expresses a state in which an expected action is not performed while the main action is carried out.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に marks the destination of movement.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 来る is in the past form 来た and serves as the main predicate.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.why: The sentence describes movement (coming to school) together with the state of not doing an action that should have been done (doing homework). It uses the linking form Vないで to connect the two parts.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It is usually used to give a cause or reason, or to connect contrasting qualities. It does not express an accompanying state like ないで.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It has a meaning similar to ないで but has a more formal written style.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q1.kobun.tip: Do not confuse Vないで (doing action 2 while in a state of not doing action 1) with Vなくて (because action 1 was not done, result 2 occurred).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vi: I had already eaten everything before he came.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject in the subordinate clause that modifies 前に.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the time noun 前.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The structure 〜前に marks the time before an action occurs.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb expressing the whole amount, modifying the action of eating.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The pattern 〜てしまいました expresses a fully completed action with a feeling of having done it unintentionally or with regret.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.why: The subordinate clause “かれが来る” modifies “前に” to set the time. It combines with the main clause using the pattern “〜てしまいました” to emphasize that all the food had already been eaten, perhaps unintentionally.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows that an action happens after something is done, completely reversing the time order from 前に.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It shows doing something beforehand as a deliberate preparation, rather than the completion or regret expressed by てしまう.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q2.kobun.tip: Before 前に, you must always use the dictionary-form verb (V辞書形), not the past form (Vた), even when the whole event happened in the past.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vi: Tomorrow I plan to go and help my friend move.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.sk: N ＋ N の ＋ N を ＋ V（drop ます）に ＋ V意向形 ＋ と思っています
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: A future-time adverb modifying the sentence predicate.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の modifies the noun ひっこし and identifies who is moving.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object of the helping action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 手伝う takes the Vます form without ます and combines with the particle に to express the purpose of movement.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 行く takes the volitional form and combines with the particle と to quote the content of the intention.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern 〜と思っています expresses a plan formed earlier and still maintained now.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.cn: Vます（drop ます）・N ＋ に行く／来る; V意向形 ＋ と思う／思っている
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.why: The sentence combines the movement-purpose structure “V（drop ます）＋ に ＋ 行く” (go in order to help) with the volitional pattern “〜と思っています” to express the speaker’s plan or intention.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It also expresses a plan, but with a stronger sense of firm decision, and is often used with the V辞書形 form.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses an intention that has just arisen at the moment of speaking, without the sense of having formed or maintained the plan as in と思っています.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q3.kobun.tip: When stating the purpose of movement—“go in order to do what?”—the verb must take the Vます form without ます and combine with に (手伝いに), not the dictionary or past form.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vi: He goes to Tokyo once a week.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N へ ＋ time period に ＋ number of times ＋ Vています
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle へ marks the direction and destination of movement.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に follows a time period to show the frequency unit.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: A counter showing how many times an action is performed within a set period.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 行く takes the ています form to express a habit or a regularly repeated action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.cn: time period ＋ に ＋ number of times ＋ V
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.why: The structure “time period + に + number of times” states a fixed frequency. Combined with the verb in the form “〜ています,” it emphasizes that the action is a regular, repeated habit.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Using the simple present would show only one future trip or a general truth, and would not highlight a repeated habit like 行っています.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: The frequency particle is used incorrectly, because Japanese requires に after the time period.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t12-q4.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse using the particle で with に when expressing a time period as the frequency standard (the correct form is 週に1回, not 週で1回).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vi: He always wears clothes that look expensive.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Adv ＋ A（remove い）そうな ＋ N を ＋ Vている
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: A frequency adverb meaning regularly, modifying the action of wearing clothes.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending in い combines with い removed and そうな to modify the noun 服 based on an outward judgment.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the direct object affected by the verb 着る.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb 着る is changed to the ている form to express the resulting state of wearing clothing on the body.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.cn: Aい（remove い）・Aな（remove な） ＋ そうな ＋ N
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.why: The sensory-judgment pattern '〜そうな' comes before the noun '服' to describe something that looks expensive. It combines with the clothing verb in the '〜ている' form to show the state of wearing clothes.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It states with certainty that the clothes are expensive, while 高そうな is only an outward-based guess.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It is used as an adverb to modify a verb, not to modify a noun directly like そうな.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q1.kobun.tip: When the judgment structure 〜そう directly modifies the following noun, the ending な (高そうな服) must be used instead of keeping the adjective ending い.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vi: I do not know whether she still likes me now.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the embedded clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: A time adverb combined with the particle も, meaning 'still even now...'
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the object toward which the feeling of liking (好き) is directed.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The structure 〜かどうか turns a clause into an embedded 'whether...or not' question that serves as the complement of the predicate.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate is in the negative form, showing that the speaker does not know the information clearly.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな（remove だ）・N（remove だ） ＋ かどうか
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.why: A choice question without a question word ('Does she like me?') is embedded as the complement of the verb 'わからない' using the pattern '〜かどうか' to express uncertainty.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Use this when the subordinate clause already contains a question word, such as いつ, だれ, or どこ, instead of a yes-or-no question.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q2.kobun.tip: When connecting an adjective ending in な or a noun with かどうか, だ must be removed (use 好きかどうか, not 好きだかどうか).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vi: If you practice, you will certainly improve.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.1.vi: if one does / if one practices
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb する is changed to the conditional 〜ば form, expressing an assumed condition that leads favorably to a result.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending in な changes to に to modify the verb なる, which shows a change of state.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb shows a change and provides the basis for modifying the judgment はずです.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The grammar pattern 〜はずです comes at the end of the sentence and expresses a confident judgment based on logic or reliable evidence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.why: The first clause gives the assumed condition 'れんしゅうをすれば'. The second clause uses the state-change phrase 'じょうずになる' with the judgment ending 'はずです' to state that the natural result will inevitably occur.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses a vague, uncertain guess (one may improve), unlike はずです, which shows confidence based on a rule or evidence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It is used for the speaker's personal intention, not for an objective logical judgment about the result.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.tip: Do not use はずだ / はずです to express the speaker's own will, determination, or personal promise.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q3.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな（な）・N（の） ＋ はずだ / はずです
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vi: Excuse me, may I take this leftover food home?
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: A phrase used to begin a polite utterance and get the other person's attention before making a request or asking a question.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: A demonstrative that directly modifies the noun for the dish (料理) that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The past-tense verb forms a clause modifying the noun 料理 and clarifies the quality of the food.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of taking it home.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb in the て form connects the action of carrying with the following action of going home.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb is nominalized with こと and combined with the particle が, which marks the possible action of the verb できます.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.ch.6.n: The potential-form predicate combines with the question particle か to ask for permission or about the possibility of doing something.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.why: The clause '残した' modifies '料理' to clearly identify the object. It combines the linked verb phrase '持って帰る' with the potential structure '〜ことができる' in polite question form to ask permission politely.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It asks another person for permission to do something, while ことができますか focuses more on whether the action is possible or allowed.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It is used to request or ask the other person to do something, so it is not suitable when the speaker wants to do it personally.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.tip: The verb before ことができる must always be in the dictionary form (V-ru). It cannot be in the past or ます form before こと.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t13-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形 ＋ ことができる
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.vi: Because my department manager assigned me work, I cannot go home.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.sk: N(person) に ＋ N(thing) を ＋ V受身 ＋ ので ＋ V可能 negative
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the agent who performs the requesting action in the passive sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object of the request or assignment.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 頼む in the past passive form combines with the conjunction ので to give an objective reason.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 帰る is changed to the polite negative potential form and serves as the main predicate, showing that the speaker cannot avoid the situation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.why: The first clause uses the direct passive structure 'Nに仕事を頼まれる' with '〜ので' to form a clause giving an objective reason. This leads to the result in the second clause: being unable to go home, '帰れません'.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It is more subjective and emphasizes the speaker's feelings, while ので sounds more objective and polite.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses actively asking for and appreciating someone's help ('having someone do something for you'), unlike 頼まれた, which means being assigned work by a superior.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.tip: In a passive sentence, the person who assigns the work or performs the action always takes the particle に (部長に), not が or を.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q1.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな（な）・N（な） ＋ ので
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vi: While I was talking with my friend, my wallet was stolen.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle と marks the person who participates with the speaker in the conversation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The progressive-form verb 〜ている modifies the noun 間 and shows that the background action is continuing.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern 〜間に connects a clause to an unexpected event that interrupts the earlier action while it is happening.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks the possession that is lost in an indirect or affected passive sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb in the polite past passive form describes the theft of an item, causing trouble and loss for the subject (迷惑受身).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.why: The first clause uses 'Vている間に' to establish a period during which the action of talking continues. The second clause uses the affected passive verb 'ぬすまれました' to describe a sudden incident that happens instantly during that period.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: The second clause must describe an action that continues throughout the entire period in the first clause, not an event that happens at one moment like 間に.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It has the sense of taking the chance to do something before a state changes or a natural event develops, rather than simply describing an interruption at one moment like 間に.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.tip: Distinguish 間, where the second clause continues throughout the period, from 間に, where the second clause is a brief, instantaneous action or event.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q2.kobun.cn: Vている・V辞書形・Aい・Aな（な）・N（の） ＋ 間に
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vi: I maintain the habit of saying thank you once a day.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.sk: N(time) に ＋ 数量 ＋ 引用 と ＋ V辞書形 ＋ ことにしている
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に follows a noun for a time period and sets the standard unit for measuring frequency.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: A counter showing how many times an action occurs, modifying the predicate.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle と is used to quote the direct words 'thank you'.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the phrase ことにしている that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The grammar pattern 〜ことにしている expresses a habit or rule that the speaker personally sets and maintains regularly.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.why: The phrase '一日に一回' sets the frequency, 'ありがとうと' quotes the content of the words and goes with the verb '言う', and the sentence ends with '〜ことにしている' to express a personal rule that is being maintained.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It describes a general rule or custom of a group, or something arranged by another person, rather than a habit that the speaker consciously sets.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It only describes a decision made at the time of speaking ('I have decided to...'), and does not yet mean maintaining a long-term habit like ことにしている.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.tip: Avoid confusing ことにしている, a habit personally decided and maintained, with ことになっている, a rule or plan set by an organization or another person.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q3.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない ＋ ことにしている
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vi: I want to return to my country during the summer vacation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The suffix 〜中に combines with the particle に to show the period during which the action takes place.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle へ shows the direction of movement toward the speaker's home country.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The ending 〜たい attaches to the V-masu stem and expresses the speaker's wish.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.why: The particle に follows the time-period phrase 夏休み中 to limit the time during which the action takes place. It combines with the direction particle へ and the desire ending 〜たい.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t14-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 夏休みの間に is used, the focus is on the period when an event occurs while the summer vacation continues.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t15-q1.kobun.vi: It has been decided that my father will buy me a new computer.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vi: That young teacher has just graduated from university.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes the teacher the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を goes with the verb 出る to show the starting point or place left.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t15-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The past-tense V-ta verb combines with ばかり to create a structure expressing an action that happened just recently.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is changed to 出たところです, it emphasizes the moment just after completion in actual time.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t15-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 出たばかりで is used, the sentence continues with another clause explaining a reason or background.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t15-q3.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse 〜たばかり, meaning 'just recently' based on subjective feeling, with 〜たところ, meaning something has just finished at that exact moment.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vi: When summer comes, perhaps even unpleasant things will all be forgotten.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb in the conditional form 〜ば expresses a natural condition related to time.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The past form of the adjective ending in な directly modifies the noun こと.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The noun こと combines with the particle も to act as the emphasized object for the following verb.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The dictionary-form verb acts as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The ending 〜でしょう expresses the speaker's gentle guess or assumption.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is changed to 来ると, it emphasizes a more inevitable result based on an obvious rule.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.tip: When the adjective ending in な is in the past form and modifies a noun, it must use 〜だった instead of keeping な.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q1.kobun.cn: Vば形・Aいければ・Aなら（ば）・Nなら（ば）
default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.vi: There are many things I have to do before tomorrow.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle 「が」 marks the subject used with the existence verb 「ある」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The quantity adverb modifies the degree of the predicate 「ある」 at the end of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The predicate indicates the existence of an inanimate thing.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse 「まで」, which means an action continues for a period, with 「までに」, which means the deadline for completing an action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vi: If you have just recovered from a cold, you should not overwork yourself.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: 「〜たところ」 emphasizes an objectively just-finished point in time and does not include the speaker's subjective feeling like 「〜たばかり」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It is used to advise what someone should do, unlike 「〜ないほうがいい」, which advises what someone should not do.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.tip: Learners often incorrectly use the dictionary form 「Vる ＋ ほうがいい」 instead of the past form 「Vた / Vない ＋ ほうがいい」 when giving advice.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t16-q3.kobun.cn: Vた ＋ ばかり / ばかりだ / ばかりなら
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q1.kobun.vi: It is very interesting, yet no one is willing to listen to my story.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The degree adverb modifies the adjective 「おもしろい」 that follows.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle 「の」 connects to modify the noun 「話」 that follows.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb takes the ending 「〜たがらない」 to show that a third person is unwilling to do something.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q2.kobun.vi: The name 「Hana」 is certainly a very Japanese name, isn't it?

default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern 「らしい」 expresses a typical quality associated with Japanese people and modifies the noun 「名前」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The noun predicate combines with the modal particle 「ね」 to seek agreement.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q2.kobun.cn: N / Aい / Aな / V普通形 ＋ らしい
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vi: This is a magazine that women in their 20s are reading.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative pronoun combines with the particle 「は」 to state the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle 「の」 connects to modify the noun 「女性」, which refers to an age group.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle 「に」 marks the agent performing the action in a passive sentence.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The noun predicate ends the sentence in the polite form.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: The causative form means making or allowing someone to read, unlike the passive form, which means that the magazine is being read.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q4.kobun.tip: Learners often incorrectly use the particle 「を」 or 「で」 instead of 「に」 when identifying the agent in a passive sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vi: Oh, that button is about to come off.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: An interjection used to express surprise and attract the other person's attention.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The subject refers to an object about to change state and is accompanied by the particle が.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb とれる, with ます removed, combines with そうだ to express an intuitive prediction about something that is about to happen before one's eyes.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.cn: V（stem ます / remove ます）・Aい（remove い）・Aな（remove な） ＋ そうだ
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.why: The speaker sees the button's current condition—it is loose—and intuitively predicts that it is about to come off. The intransitive verb「とれる」in the form with「ます」removed combines with「そう」to show a sign that something is about to happen.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If the plain form「とれるそうだ」is used, the sentence means that the speaker heard someone say the button will come off.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q1.kobun.tip: Do not confuse the form describing a situation about to happen「V(remove ます)＋そうだ」(about to come off) with the reported-information form「V(base form)＋そうだ」(heard that it will come off).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vi: Since the rain does not look likely to stop, I will take a taxi home.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: A strong negative form of そうだ, showing that the rain is very unlikely to stop.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: A conjunction showing an objective cause that leads to the decision in the following clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle で indicates the means of transportation.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It has the same meaning and usage, but「そうもない」emphasizes slightly more strongly that something is completely unlikely to happen.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It is the negative form of an adjective when combined with そう. It is not used for a verb expressing a possibility judgment like「やみそうもない」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q2.kobun.tip: The pattern「〜そうもない」only combines with a verb with ますremoved to express a low possibility. Learners often confuse it with the dictionary form or use the wrong particle.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vi: I have been eating too much lately, so I will not eat lunch today.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The main predicate is a polite negative form describing an action that will not be performed.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It describes a general rule or an excessively strong general quality (“because one eats too much, ...”), so it is less natural than the nominalized form when discussing a recent condition.
