default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vi: I am embarrassed because my handwriting is very bad.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object being evaluated by the adjective 下手.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending in な removes な and combines with すぎて in the て form to connect to the clause expressing the reason.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The main predicate expresses the speaker's feeling of embarrassment.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.cn: V(remove ます)・Aい(remove い)・Aな(remove な) ＋ すぎる
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.why: The sentence states the topic as わたしは. The subordinate clause then uses 〜すぎて to give the reason—the handwriting is too bad—which leads to the main clause はずかしいです expressing embarrassment.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 下手で is used, it simply means “because the handwriting is bad” and does not emphasize an excessive degree beyond normal, unlike 下手すぎて.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: If 下手そう is used, it means an appearance-based guess (“looks clumsy/bad”), so it is not suitable when talking about one's own fact.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q4.kobun.tip: When the adjective ending in な combines with すぎる, な must be removed (下手すぎて). Learners often incorrectly keep な or use the wrong form.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vi: My husband is too busy and is hardly ever at home.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the husband as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective いそがしい drops い and combines with すぎます to show that the level of being busy exceeds the normal limit.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb of degree that is used with a following negative verb to express “hardly ever.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に shows the place where a person exists with the verbs います/いません.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: A polite negative predicate expressing that someone is not present at home.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.cn: V(drop ます)・Aい(drop い)・Aな(drop な) ＋ すぎる
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.why: The first sentence uses the pattern すぎます to emphasize the husband’s excessive busyness. The second sentence uses the adverb あまり with the negative verb いません to state the actual result caused by being too busy.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If とてもいそがしい is used, it only has the objective meaning “very busy,” while いそがしすぎます has a negative nuance, meaning busy beyond the acceptable limit.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q5.kobun.tip: When the い-ending adjective combines with すぎる, it must drop the ending い (いそがしすぎます). Learners often forget this and keep い unchanged.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vi: It is difficult to talk when everyone is listening. Let’s talk privately, just the two of us.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.sk: N が ＋ Vていると ＋ V(drop ます)＋にくいです。N だけで ＋ Vましょう
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject performing the action in the conditional clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The ている form of the verb combines with the particle と to form a conditional clause describing the situation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 話す drops ます and combines with にくいです to express that speaking is difficult and involves many obstacles.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle だけ (“only”) combines with the particle で to indicate the scope or size of the group performing the action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: The ending ましょう is used to make an invitation or suggest a solution.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.why: The first clause uses と to state the condition (everyone is listening) that makes speaking difficult (話しにくい). Therefore, the second sentence uses 二人だけで ＋ 話しましょう to invite the other person to talk privately.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: 話しづらい strongly expresses the speaker’s feeling of embarrassment and awkwardness, while 話しにくい is more objective about the difficulty of speaking.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 話せない is used, it means completely “cannot speak” (the negative potential form), while 話しにくい means that speaking is still possible but involves many obstacles.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q6.kobun.tip: The pattern 〜にくい is used only with the ます form of a verb, dropping ます (話しにくい). Learners often mistakenly combine it with the dictionary form (話すにくい).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vi: An expensive watch is difficult to break. The previous watch was cheap, so it broke immediately.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.sk: Aい ＋ N は ＋ V(drop ます)＋にくい。N の ＋ N は ＋ Aい過去＋から ＋ 副詞 ＋ Vてしまった
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The い-ending adjective directly modifies the noun 時計 that follows it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は introduces the first topic being compared in the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb こわれる drops ます and combines with にくい to describe the quality of being durable and difficult to break.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The noun 前 combines with the particle の to modify the noun 時計 (the old watch).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle は introduces the second topic being compared (the previous watch).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: The adjective 安い changes to the past form 安かった and combines with the particle から to state the reason.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: An adverb that modifies a verb and emphasizes that something happens quickly.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.ch.7.n: The verb changes to the てしまう form in the past to show that the breakage happened regretfully.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.why: The two sentences use the particle は (高い時計は ... 前の時計は) to create a contrast between the expensive watch, which is difficult to break (こわれにくい), and the old, cheap watch, which quickly broke (こわれてしまった).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: こわれやすい is the opposite pattern, expressing the quality of being “easy to break and likely to break” for an object.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q7.kobun.tip: When used with an intransitive verb (such as こわれる), 〜にくい describes the quality or nature of a thing, not the feeling that a person has difficulty performing an action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.vi: This map is really difficult to understand, isn’t it? Do you have a map that is a little easier to understand?
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.sk: 連体詞 ＋ N、 ＋ V(drop ます)＋にくいですね。副詞 ＋ 副詞 ＋ V(drop ます)＋やすい ＋ N は ＋ ありませんか
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative この directly modifies the noun 地図 that follows it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: It introduces the object being commented on, with the particle は omitted in informal speech.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: V(drop ます) ＋ にくい expresses the quality of being difficult to understand. It ends with the particle ね to seek agreement.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb that modifies 少し to express “a little more.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: An adverb of quantity that modifies the quality わかりやすい.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: The phrase V(drop ます) ＋ やすい functions like a い-ending adjective and directly modifies the noun 地図 that follows it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle は marks the noun as the object being asked for or searched for.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.ch.7.n: A polite negative question used to ask for an object or make a gentle request.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.cn: V(drop ます) ＋ やすい / にくい
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.why: The first sentence uses わかりにくい to comment that the map is difficult to see or understand. The second uses わかりやすい to directly modify the noun 地図 and combines it with the negative question ありませんか to look for an easier-to-understand map.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: わかりやすい is the affirmative opposite of わかりにくい and expresses the quality of being “easy to understand.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: Using only わかる地図 does not clearly express the quality of having a clear, easy-to-see design as わかりやすい地図 does.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q8.kobun.tip: The pattern 〜やすい changes a verb into a い-ending adjective. Therefore, when it modifies a following noun, it connects directly (わかりやすい地図), without adding な or の.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vi: I tend to gain weight. Therefore, I do not eat sweet foods.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.sk: N は ＋ V(drop ます)＋やすいです。接続詞、 ＋ Aい ＋ N は ＋ V否定
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the speaker as the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb 太る drops ます and combines with やすいです to express a physical tendency to become fat or gain weight easily.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: A conjunction linking sentences and showing a cause-and-effect relationship.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The い-ending adjective directly modifies the noun もの.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle は replaces を and makes the object “sweet foods” the emphasized topic of the negative sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: A polite negative verb form expressing the habit of not eating sweet foods.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.why: The first sentence uses 太りやすい to state the speaker’s physical tendency. The second begins with the cause-and-effect conjunction だから and leads to the result of avoiding sweet foods (あまいものは食べません). The particle は emphasizes the object being negated.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: 太りにくい is the opposite pattern, meaning “difficult to gain weight or become fat.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: 太りそう means that someone seems likely to gain weight soon or that a food is likely to cause weight gain. It does not express a physical tendency like 太りやすい.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t2-q9.kobun.tip: When the pattern 〜やすい is used with verbs describing change (such as 太る and 風邪をひく), it expresses a tendency to “easily become” or “often become” something, not that an action is easy to perform.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.sk: N (frequency) ＋ N (time) に ＋ N (destination) に ＋ Vています
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing how often an action is repeated.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に identifies the specific time when the action takes place.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the destination of an action of movement.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb form V-ています is used to describe regular, repeated habits.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.why: Because the sentence contains the phrases 「毎週 木よう日に」, which show a regular weekly cycle, the predicate must use 「V-ています」 to express a lifestyle habit.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「行きます」 is used, it usually only states a future event or one specific trip. It does not emphasize a lasting habit as strongly as 「行っています」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q1.kobun.tip: Learners often think that 「V-ています」 is used only for an action happening at the moment of speaking, and forget that it can also describe habits and customs.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vi: The children's picture has been put up.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects nouns and modifies the noun “picture.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object that exists in a resulting state.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.2.vi: has been put up in advance
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern V-てあります is used with a transitive verb to describe a state that remains after an intentional action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.why: The speaker wants to describe the picture as being on the wall/board as the result of someone putting it up earlier, so they use the transitive verb 「はる」 with 「〜てあります」 and the particle 「が」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: If the transitive verb 「絵をはっています」 is used, it describes someone putting up the picture at the moment of speaking.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「はりました」 is used, it only reports that the picture was put up in the past. It does not emphasize that the resulting state still remains before us.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.tip: When changing to the state pattern 「V-てあります」, the object that originally goes with を of the transitive verb changes to the particle が.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q2.kobun.cn: 他動詞Vて + あります
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vi: The rice has already been prepared. Eat quickly.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.sk: N が + 他動詞Vて + あります + よ + Aく + Vます(remove ます) + なさい
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the object that has already been prepared in the V-てあります pattern.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern V-てあります shows that something has been prepared in advance. It combines with the particle よ to inform the other person.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending い changes to the form く and becomes an adverb modifying the verb “eat.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The ending なさい creates a mild command used when a superior advises or orders a subordinate.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.cn: 他動詞Vて + あります; Vます(remove ます) + なさい
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.why: The first clause uses 「作ってあります」 to announce that the rice was fully prepared earlier. This creates the basis for the urging expression 「食べなさい」 in the second clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「作りました」 is used, it only tells us that the speaker finished cooking the rice. It does not clearly have the meaning of preparing it for someone else as 「作ってあります」 does.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「食べてください」 is used, it is a polite request, while 「食べなさい」 is a reminder from a superior to a subordinate.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q3.kobun.tip: The pattern 「V-てあります」 cannot be used with an intransitive verb. For example, saying ごはんができてあります is grammatically incorrect.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vi:
A: “Whose handkerchief is this?”
B: “Oh, there is a name written here.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.sk:
A「だれの + N + ですか。」
B「あ、N(place) に + N が + 他動詞Vて + あります + よ。」
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The question word だれ combines with the particle の to ask about ownership.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: A noun combines with ですか to form a question that identifies an object.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: An interjection showing that the speaker has suddenly realized something.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates the location where the written words exist.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks the object that exists in the V-てあります pattern.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern V-てあります describes writing that someone has already put on something to record information.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.why: Character B sees that a name has already been written on the handkerchief, showing an intentional remaining state. Therefore, they use the pattern 「Nが 書いてあります」 with the particle 「よ」 to point it out to the other person.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「書いています」 is used, it describes someone holding a pen and writing the name at the moment of speaking, rather than describing writing that is already there.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.tip: When describing writing, drawings, or information that already exists on an object, Japanese generally prefers 「〜てあります」 rather than the simple past tense.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q4.kobun.cn: 他動詞Vて + あります
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vi: I always study before going to bed.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the subject as the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb showing absolute frequency. It modifies the studying action in the predicate.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb comes before 前に to form a clause showing a point in time.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The pattern 〜まえに identifies the time before an action happens.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb form V-ています combines with the adverb いつも to describe a fixed daily habit.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.why: The pattern 「V-る前に」 must use the dictionary form to show the later action. It combines with 「いつも」 and 「勉強しています」 to express a daily habit.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: The form 「ねた前に」 is completely ungrammatical. Before 「前に」, the verb must always be in the dictionary form (辞書形).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「勉強します」 is used, the sentence still has meaning, but 「勉強しています」 shows the continuing regular habit more clearly.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q5.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly think that the later action, sleeping, should use the past tense before 前に. However, Japanese grammar always requires the dictionary form before 前に.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vi:
A: “What happened?”
B: “My mother is not answering the phone, so I am in the middle of worrying and feeling troubled.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The ending の is used in informal questions to ask about the other person's reason or situation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が identifies the subject performing the action in the subordinate clause showing the reason.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に goes with the fixed phrase 電話に出る, meaning “answer the phone.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.3.vi: is not answering the phone, so
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The negative verb changes to the form なく-て to connect a clause showing a reason.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: V-ている modifies the noun ところ to show a continuing difficult situation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.5.vi: right in the middle of it.」
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern 〜ところだ combines with the explanatory ending 〜なんです to explain the current situation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.why: The speaker uses the reason-linking clause 「出なくて」 and the pattern 「V-ているところなんです」 to explain that they are right in the middle of this troubling situation at the time they are asked.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If 「こまっていたところ」 is used, it means that the speaker has just escaped from the trouble in the past, and it is no longer continuing now.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If 「こまっているからです」 is used, it simply gives the reason. It lacks the immediate feeling of “being in this situation right now” found in 「〜ところなんです」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q6.kobun.tip: The pattern 「V-ているところ」 emphasizes an action or state happening right at the moment of speaking. This differs from 「V-るところ」, meaning “about to happen,” and 「V-たところ」, meaning “just finished.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vi: I am sorry that my children are so noisy.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.sk: N が + Aい(remove い)くて、 + すみません
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject causing the noisy state.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending い changes to the form て to give the reason for the apology that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The main predicate expresses an apology for an inconvenient situation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.cn: Vて・Aい(remove い)くて・Aな/Nで + すみません／ありがとう
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.why: The first clause uses the adjective form て (うるさくて) to show the reason for the apology (すみません) in the second clause. It also uses the particle が to mark the subject causing the noise.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It gives the reason directly, so it sounds less gentle and less natural when used with an apology.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: It changes the meaning into a complaint about the inconvenience instead of an apology.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q7.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly use から instead of the form て when giving a reason for an apology or thanks.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vi: This pen is expensive, but it is very easy to write with.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.sk: N は + Aい + が + 副詞 + V(remove ます)やすいです
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative directly modifies the noun ペン that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the topic being evaluated or commented on.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が connects two clauses with contrasting meanings.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb of degree modifying the adjective predicate that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: A verb in the ます form, with ます removed, combines with やすい to express that writing is easy and smooth.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.cn: V(with ます removed) ＋ やすい (conjugated like an い-ending adjective)
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.why: The pattern やすい is attached directly to the ます-form verb stem to create an い-ending adjective meaning that something is easy to do. The conjunction particle が links the contrast between price and the experience of using it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: It has the completely opposite meaning, “difficult to write.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: It emphasizes that the act of writing is simple, rather than that writing feels smooth and comfortable.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q8.kobun.tip: Do not confuse attaching やすい with the dictionary-form verb. For example, 書くやすい is incorrect; it must be changed to 書きやすい.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vi: These clothes are too large. Do you have size M or S?
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Aい(with い removed)すぎます。N か ＋ N は ＋ ありますか
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative directly modifies the noun 服.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the topic of the sentence to be commented on.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The い-ending adjective, with い removed, combines with すぎます to show that something exceeds a suitable limit.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle か lists the first choice.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle は follows the choices to emphasize the topic whose existence is being asked about.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The interrogative predicate asks whether the item is present or available.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.cn: V(with ます removed)・Aい(with い removed)・Aな ＋ すぎる／すぎます
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.why: The pattern すぎる follows the い-ending adjective stem, with い removed, to express a state that exceeds what is necessary. The next sentence uses か to connect the choices and は to make those choices the topic of the question.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: It simply describes a large size and does not have the negative sense of being inconveniently too large.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses the past tense, so it is not suitable when trying on clothes and asking to change the size immediately.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t3-q9.kobun.tip: Learners often forget to remove the い ending of the adjective when combining it with すぎる. Writing 大きいすぎます is incorrect; it must be 大きすぎます.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vi: In winter, my dog refuses to go for walks at all.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.sk: N の ＋ N は、 ＋ 時期 は ＋ N に ＋ V(with ます removed)たがらない
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects a noun showing possession and modifies 犬.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は marks the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は marks a time topic and contrasts it with other times.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に follows a noun that shows the purpose of movement.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb changes to the たがる pattern in the negative form to describe a third person's expression of desire.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.cn: V(with ます removed) ＋ たがる／たがらない (used for the third person and conjugated like a group 1 verb)
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.why: The subject carrying out the action is a third person (the dog), so when expressing this subject's feelings or wishes, the ending たがる must be used and changed to the negative form たがらない.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Used directly for the speaker's own wishes (the first person), so it is unnatural to apply it directly to another person.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It only states the fact that the dog does not go for a walk and does not show that the dog is reluctant or unwilling to go.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q1.kobun.tip: Avoid using たい or たくない to talk about another person's or an animal's wishes or inner feelings without a word showing uncertainty.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vi: I have a test tomorrow, so I want you to keep quiet. I cannot study at all.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A time noun used as an adverb to show when an event takes place.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle から follows a noun with だ to give the reason for the request that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.2.vi: I want you to keep quiet.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The structure てほしい expresses the speaker's wish for the listener to keep quiet.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb used with a negative predicate to emphasize that there is no progress at all.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks the subject of the intransitive verb 進む.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: A negative-form intransitive verb expressing that something is not going smoothly or is not sinking in.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ ほしい (expresses the wish for another person to do V for the speaker)
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.why: The first clause uses てほしい to express the wish for the listener to act (to keep quiet), because of the test (だから). The next sentence uses the adverb ぜんぜん with a negative form to emphasize the stuck situation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It means that the speaker wants to keep quiet, not that the speaker is asking the listener to do so.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It is a direct request or command, while てほしい expresses a thought or wish more gently.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse たい (what the speaker wants to do) with てほしい (what the speaker wants another person to do for them).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vi: I want to become a singer someday.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 副詞 ＋ N に ＋ V(with ます removed)たい
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the first-person subject expressing the speaker's own wish.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb showing an unspecified time in the future.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に accompanies the verb なる to show the result of a change or becoming.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb なる changes to the たい form to express the speaker's own wish.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.cn: V(with ます removed) ＋ たい (used for the first person and conjugated like an い-ending adjective)
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.why: The topic is the first person, わたし, so the pattern たい is used to express the speaker's dream directly. It combines with the particle に and the verb なる, which shows a change of profession.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Used to describe a third person's wish, not the speaker's own wish わたし.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses a more specific plan or intention than a dream or feeling such as たい.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q3.kobun.tip: Remember that the particle used with the verb なる when changing a profession or state is に (歌手になる), not を.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vi: Micchan really wanted to become a singer in the past, didn't she?
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.sk: N は ＋ 時点 ＋ N に ＋ Vます形（with ます）たがっていた removed ＋ ね
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the person being discussed the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: A time adverb referring to the past and modifying the entire predicate that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に accompanies a noun showing the result of a change with the verb なる.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.3.vi: used to want to become one, didn't she?
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb なる combines with the ending たがる in the past progressive tense to express a third person's wish in the past.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.cn: Vます形（with ます） removed ＋ たがる / たがっている / たがっていた
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.why: Because the subject is Micchan (the third person) and the event continued for a period in the past, the sentence must use the structure 〜たがっていた instead of 〜たい, which is used only for the first person.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Used directly only for the wishes of the first person, meaning the speaker. Using it for another person in a statement sounds unnatural.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: It shows an inference based on someone's appearance at the time of observation, not another person's lasting wish.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q4.kobun.tip: Avoid using 〜たい directly when talking about another person's wish in a statement. Change it to 〜たがる or 〜たいと言っている.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vi: He never seems to go home. I wish he would go home soon...
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the topic of the first statement.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The adverb なかなか is used with a negative form to emphasize that something does not happen as expected.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: A possessive noun phrase modifying the place noun immediately after it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle へ shows the direction and destination of the act of returning.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: A negative-form verb expressing that an action still has not been carried out.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: An adverb showing that it is the appropriate time for an action to happen.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.6.vi: I want him to go home...
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: The grammar pattern Vてほしい is used by the speaker to express a wish for another person to carry out an action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.why: The first clause uses なかなか with a negative form to emphasize the unpleasant delay. The second clause uses Vてほしい because the speaker wants the other person to go home.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It only expresses the speaker's wish to do something, not a wish for another person to do it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses the speaker's wish to do something that benefits another person.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.tip: Clearly distinguish Vたい (the speaker wants to do something) from Vてほしい (the speaker wants the listener or a third person to do something).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q5.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ ほしい / ほしくない
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vi: Nao can speak as many as four languages. That is really impressive, isn't it?
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the person being praised the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle も follows a quantity word to emphasize that the amount is greater than usual.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb 話す is changed into the polite potential form 話せます.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.3.vi: That is really impressive, isn't it?
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective combines with the ending ですね to form an exclamatory sentence that gives praise and seeks agreement.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.why: The speaker uses the particle も after the number '４か国語' instead of an objective particle to show amazement, together with the potential verb and the praising exclamation that follow.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It suggests a disappointingly small amount, completely opposite to the particle も, which emphasizes a large amount.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: It states the quantity objectively and neutrally, without showing surprise or emotion.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q6.kobun.tip: When the particle も comes directly after a quantity word, it replaces を/が and emphasizes the meaning 'as many as / as much as'.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vi: I can speak only Japanese. I cannot speak either English or Chinese.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.sk: N は ＋ N しか ＋ V可能形（negative）。N も ＋ N も ＋ できません。
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the speaker the topic and limits the scope of their ability.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle しか limits the meaning to this one object and must be combined with a negative ending.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The potential verb is changed into the negative form and combined with しか to mean that the speaker can speak only Japanese.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle も lists the first object whose possibility is denied.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle も lists the second object, which shares the same negative state.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.5.vi: cannot / do not know how to.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb できる is changed into the negative form to show a lack of ability in the listed languages.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.why: The first sentence uses the structure 'N + しか + negative V' to emphasize exclusivity with a modest, limited tone. The second uses 'も...も...ない' to deny all the other foreign languages.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It can be used with an affirmative sentence (日本語だけ話せます) and only states an objective fact, without the regretful or complaining tone of しか.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q7.kobun.tip: The structure 〜しか requires the predicate ending to always be in the negative form (〜ない/〜ません).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q7.tokens.8.m: cannot / do not know how to
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vi: Last night, I could sleep for only three hours.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing a point in past time that sets the context for the action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle しか attaches to a duration word to emphasize an unsatisfyingly small amount.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.2.vi: did not sleep (could sleep only that long).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb is changed into the negative past tense to match the particle しか before it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.cn: Number word (数量詞) ＋ しか ＋ V否定形
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.why: The particle しか comes directly after the counter '３時間' and combines with the negative past predicate to express insufficient sleep and complain about the very short period.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If '３時間だけねました' is used, the sentence simply reports objectively that the speaker slept for three hours, without a complaining or deprived feeling.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If '３時間も' is used, it emphasizes that the duration is very long, 'as many as three hours,' which is completely opposite to the context.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q8.kobun.tip: Although the predicate is in the negative form (ねませんでした), when it is used with しか, the sentence means affirmatively 'could sleep for only three hours.'
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vi: Thank you so much for coming today.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は makes the time point the topic and limits the context of the thanks.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.1.vi: for coming to help me and
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb くる in the て form combines with くれる to show that the other person's action brings joy to the speaker and connects to the thanks.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb that modifies the sentence and emphasizes the sincerity of the thanks that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The predicate ends the sentence and expresses gratitude in a familiar, informal way.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.why: The Vてくれて structure states an action that the listener has done for the speaker. It serves as the direct reason connected to the thanks ありがとう.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: It describes doing an action for someone else, so it cannot be used when another person does something for oneself as an act to be thanked for.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: It also expresses receiving an action, but it suggests that the speaker asked for it beforehand, while 〜てくれて emphasizes the other person's willingness and enthusiasm.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.tip: When thanking someone for doing something for you, the most accurate and natural patterns are 'Vてくれてありがとう' in informal speech or 'Vてくださってありがとうございます' in polite speech.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t4-q9.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ くれる / くれて / ください
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vi:
A: 「Oh, I forgot my textbook!」
B: 「Then, I will show you mine.」
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: An interjection showing A's surprise upon realizing that they forgot something.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The direct object of the action of forgetting. The particle を is omitted in spoken language.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: A short-form past predicate describing the realization that an action has already happened accidentally.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: A linking word that begins the reply and introduces a helpful solution.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: A possessive pronoun combined with the particle を as the object of the action of showing.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.5.vi: I will show it to you.」
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern 〜てあげる shows that the speaker willingly does something kind to help the other person.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.why: Person B uses the giving-and-receiving structure 「〜てあげる」 because the action comes from the speaker and provides help or a benefit to the listener.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Used when another person does something beneficial for the speaker. It is not used when the speaker helps another person.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: Used when the speaker receives help from someone after asking for it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q1.kobun.tip: Be careful when using 「〜てあげる」 with superiors or strangers because this structure can sound like claiming credit for doing them a favor.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vi: I am having trouble. Could you give me some advice?
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: A progressive-form predicate describing a current difficult situation as the basis for asking for help.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: An indefinite word that modifies the noun that follows by expressing quantity or degree.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle を marks the direct object of the giving-and-receiving action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The polite negative form of くれる used to make a request and ask the other person for help.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.cn: N を ＋ くれる / くれませんか（or Vて ＋ くれませんか）
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.why: The speaker first states their difficult situation, then uses the polite negative question 「〜くれませんか」 to ask the other person to act for them or help them.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It means inviting someone to do something together or offering to do something for them. It is not used to ask to receive a favor.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: This form is not used to make a direct request. It must be changed into the potential form 〜てもらえませんか.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q2.kobun.tip: Avoid confusing the direction of 「くれる」 (an action directed toward me) with 「あげる」 (an action directed from me toward another person).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vi: I do not understand this problem. I will ask the teacher to explain it to me.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.sk: N1 が ＋ わからない ＋ N2(person) に ＋ Vてもらおう
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: A demonstrative word placed before and directly modifying the noun 問題.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が marks the object that is not understood with the stative verb わからない.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: A short-form negative predicate describing a state of not understanding the knowledge clearly.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates the person affected by the action or the person from whom the speaker receives a favor.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.4.vi: I will ask them to teach me.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The structure 〜てもらう is changed into the volitional form to express the decision or intention to ask the other person to teach the speaker.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.why: When facing a problem they do not understand, the speaker decides to seek help from the teacher by using the volitional form of the receiving-a-favor pattern 「〜てもらう」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses the speaker's intention to do something kind for the teacher, which is completely wrong for the roles and context.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: This volitional form does not exist when the speaker expresses their own intention.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.tip: In the structure 「〜てもらう」, the person who performs the helpful action must be accompanied by the particle 「に」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q3.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ もらう / もらおう
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vi: I overworked myself and became ill.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.sk: N は ＋ Vます(omit ます) ＋ すぎて ＋ V(result)
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は establishes the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The verb omits ます and combines with すぎる in the て form to make a linking clause showing an excessive cause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に shows the result of a change in physical condition used with the verb なる.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: A polite past predicate confirming that a change in health condition occurred.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.cn: Vます(remove ます)・Aい(remove い)・Aな ＋ すぎる
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.why: The pattern 「〜すぎる」 expresses an action that goes beyond a reasonable limit. It uses the て form (すぎて) to connect the cause leading to the negative result of becoming ill in the following clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Describes two actions happening in parallel at the same time, without expressing a cause-and-effect relationship involving excess.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: Describes a judgment based on appearance, not on an actual action that went beyond the limit.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q4.kobun.tip: The verb combined with 「〜すぎる」 must drop the ending ます (働きます → 働きすぎて); it does not keep the dictionary form.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vi: As for the homework, let us finish all of it within this year.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は puts the noun “homework” at the beginning of the sentence as the topic to be dealt with.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: A time noun combines with the particle の to modify the noun うち.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The structure 〜うちに combines with the particle に to show that the time should be used before the year ends.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: Combines 〜てしまう (complete finishing) with the volitional form (〜よう) to encourage the speaker to finish.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.why: The structure 「〜うちに」 shows that the remaining time before the new year should be used. It combines with the volitional predicate 「〜てしまおう」 to express the determination to finish the task completely.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Only indicates an action taking place during a specified period; it does not emphasize making use of an opportunity like うちに.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: Only indicates the deadline by which something must be completed. It is more compulsory than making use of time before conditions change.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.tip: When combined with a noun, the pattern 「うちに」 must add the particle 「の」 (e.g., 今年のうちに).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q5.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vている・Vない・Aい・Aな・Nの ＋ うちに
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vi: When you graduate, do not forget me.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: Vたら creates a conditional or time clause, meaning when or after graduating.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the person who is remembered.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: Vないでね is used to ask or tell someone not to do something.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.why: The clause 卒業したら comes first to state the time or condition. The object of 忘れる is marked with を, while 忘れないでね is a gentle reminder at the end of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: If it replaced this pattern, the sentence would be closer to a certain condition or an inevitable result, so it would not fit a direct reminder as well.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: If ね is omitted, the sentence is still a request, but it sounds more direct and less friendly.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 忘れなくて instead of 忘れないで, but the pattern for asking someone not to do something is Vないで.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q6.kobun.cn: Vた形 ＋ ら; Vない形 ＋ でね
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vi: After appearing in that movie, Mr. Tanaka became famous.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies Mr. Tanaka as the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The demonstrative directly modifies the following noun, “movie.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に indicates the place or work in which the subject performs.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 出る changes to the て form to connect a sequence of events and show the cause leading to the following result.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The adjective ending な changes to に to combine with the verb なる, which indicates a change of state.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: A past-tense predicate describing a completed change of state.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.cn: Aな ＋ になる / N ＋ になる / Aい (remove い) ＋ くなる
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.why: The sentence uses the て form to connect events in time order and show a cause-and-effect relationship. It then applies the state-change pattern「Aな ＋ になる」to state the result after appearing in the movie.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: This is grammatically incorrect because 有名 is an adjective ending in な. It must use 有名になる, not change to the ending く like an adjective ending in い.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q7.kobun.tip: Learners often mistake the ending of an adjective ending in な for く (such as 有名くなる) when changing it with なる.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q7.tokens.1.m: Mr., Ms., or another polite title
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q7.tokens.6.m: to appear; to act in a movie
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.vi:
Child: "Mom, please give me that game for my birthday. Is that okay?"
Mother: "Ask Dad to buy it for you."
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.sk: N(the person who performs the action) に ＋ Vて ＋ もらう
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: Indicates the speaker of the first line.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: A form of address used to get the mother's attention.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle の indicates possession and modifies the noun “birthday.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle に indicates a point in time and combines with は to emphasize the birthday occasion.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The demonstrative modifies the game that both people already know about.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle が goes with the object of the adjective expressing desire, ほしい.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: The adjective ほしい expresses the speaker's desire to own something and is followed by the exclamatory particle な.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.7.n: Used to ask for permission or confirm agreement.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.8.n: Indicates the speaker of the following reply.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.9.n: The particle に indicates the person asked to perform the action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.10.vi: Ask him to buy it for you.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.ch.10.n: The pattern 〜てもらう in the て form is used to give advice or ask the child to ask the father to buy it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.why: The mother tells the child to ask the father to buy the gift for the child. Therefore, it uses the receiving-action pattern「〜てもらう」with the person performing the action marked by the particle に.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: It would mean telling the child to buy a gift for the father, which is completely opposite to the child's meaning of receiving something from the father.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the particle に with を, which marks the person performing the action in the pattern 〜てもらう.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q8.kobun.cn: Vて ＋ もらう / いただく
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vi:
A: "Do you know where my glasses are?"
B: "I don't know. Try looking more carefully."
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.sk: Question word question ＋ か ＋ 知らない？
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: Indicates the person asking where the item is.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の modifies the noun “glasses.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun is made the topic of the question, with the particle は omitted in casual conversation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The question word combines with the particle に to indicate a location.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle か embeds a question with a question word as a clause modifying the following verb of knowledge.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb 知る in the negative form is used to ask whether the other person knows the information.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: Indicates the person replying to the question.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: The negative verb shows that the speaker does not have the information and is combined with よ for emphasis.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.8.n: An adverb of degree modifying the following adverb よく.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.9.n: An adverb of manner modifying the verb “search.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.ch.10.n: The pattern 〜てみる in the て form is used to advise someone to try an action and see what happens.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.cn: Question sentence (plain form / だ omitted) ＋ か ＋ 知る/分からない
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.why: A embeds the question about the location「どこにあるか」as the object of「知らない？」to ask whether B knows. B does not know the information, so B answers with「知らない」and advises the friend to search again using「〜てみて」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: This is grammatically incorrect because Japanese always uses 知らない for the state of not knowing information, not 知っていない.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t5-q9.kobun.tip: Learners often translate “currently do not know” as 知っていない, but the standard rule is always to use 知らない.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vi:
A: "The TV is on."
B: "The news will start soon, so just leave it on."
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.sk: N が + intransitive V ている / transitive V て + おく
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: Only the person who notices and reports the TV's state.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が goes with the intransitive verb and marks the subject of the state of being on.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The intransitive verb つく in the 〜ている form describes the state of the TV being on.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: Only the person who receives the information and makes a request.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: An adverb showing that an event will happen very soon.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle が marks the subject of the action that will begin.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle から connects the sentence and expresses the reason why the news program will start soon.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.ch.7.n: The transitive verb つける combines with 〜ておく to show that the TV is kept on in preparation for watching it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.why: A states the TV's objective condition with the intransitive verb 「つく + ている」, while B intentionally wants to maintain that condition in preparation for watching the news, so B uses the transitive verb 「つける + ておく」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: This is wrong because the structure 〜ておく, which expresses intentional preparation or maintenance, is used only with the transitive verb つける and cannot combine with the intransitive verb つく.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q1.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the pair of the intransitive verb (つく - a natural state) and the transitive verb (つける - an intentional action when used with 〜ておく).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vi:
A: "Your wallet is in my bag."
B: "Oh, I see. But we are going shopping together later, so just leave it in there."
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.sk: N が + intransitive V ている / transitive V て + おく
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: Only the person who discovers and reports the object.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle の modifies the noun meaning bag.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the place where the object is contained.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle の modifies the noun meaning wallet.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle が marks the object that is inside the bag.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: The intransitive verb はいる in the 〜ていた form describes the state of already being in the bag.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: Only the person who responds to the information.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.7.n: An interjection showing that the information has been received.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.8.n: A conjunction that changes direction and introduces the reason for the following request.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.9.n: A noun phrase showing the time when the action will take place.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.10.n: An adverb showing that the action is done together.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.11.n: A noun combined with the particle に to express the purpose of going.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.12.n: The particle から gives the reason for leaving the wallet in the bag.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.ch.13.n: The transitive verb いれる combines with 〜ておく and means keeping the wallet in its current place in preparation for the next shopping trip.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.why: A reports that the wallet is already in the bag, using the intransitive verb はいっていた, while B wants it to remain there so it can be used later, so B makes a request with the transitive verb 「いれておいて」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: This is grammatically wrong because the pattern 〜ておく describes intentional preparation, so it must use the transitive verb いれる and cannot be used with the intransitive verb はいる.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q2.kobun.tip: Learners often confuse the intransitive verb はいる, meaning that something is already inside, and the transitive verb いれる, meaning that someone intentionally puts something inside, when they are used with 〜ておく.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vi:
A: "Huh? The ice cream is outside the freezer."
B: "I want to soften it before eating it, so just leave it outside."
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.sk: N が + intransitive V ている / transitive V て + おく
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: Only the person who notices an unusual situation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: An interjection showing surprise at what the speaker sees.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle から marks the starting point, the place from which the object was taken out.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle が marks the subject of the state of being outside the freezer.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The state of an object being outside on its own is expressed by the intransitive verb 出ている.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: Only the person who explains the purpose and makes a request.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: The adjective やわらかい in the 〜くして form describes the intentional action of making the ice cream soft.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.7.vi: because I want to eat it,
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: The desire form たい combined with から gives the reason for taking out the ice cream.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.ch.8.n: The transitive verb 出す combines with 〜ておく to show intentionally leaving the ice cream outside the freezer in preparation for eating it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.why: In sentence A, the speaker sees that the ice cream is outside the freezer, so the intransitive verb 「出ている」 is used. In sentence B, the speaker intends to soften the ice cream before eating it, so the transitive verb 「出しておく」 is used to request that this prepared state be maintained.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It describes an action that someone intentionally prepared earlier and whose result is still being maintained, unlike a request to leave it as it is 「出しておいて」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.tip: The intransitive verb 出る, used with ている to describe a state, must be clearly distinguished from the transitive verb 出す, used with ておく for purposeful preparation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q3.kobun.cn: Vて + いる / Vて + おく
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.sk: N (person causing harm) に + N (possessed object) を + V受身
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に marks the person who directly causes the troublesome action in an indirect passive sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks an object negatively affected that belongs to the subject.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb こわす changes to the passive form こわされる in the polite past tense to show that the speaker suffered harm.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.cn: Group 1 verbs (a-row + れる) / Group 2 verbs (remove る + られる) / Group 3 verbs (される / こられる)
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.why: This sentence uses the indirect passive structure to express the subject's annoyance and loss when another person damages an object that belongs to the subject.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It simply reports that the child broke the computer, without showing that the speaker suffered any loss.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q4.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly make the object the subject instead of keeping the person who suffered the loss as the subject.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vi: Officer! My wallet has been stolen!
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: A call used to get the other person's attention before reporting the incident.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the speaker's stolen property.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb ぬすむ changes to the passive form ぬすまれる in the polite past tense to show the loss caused by someone stealing it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.cn: Group 1 verbs (a-row + れる) / Group 2 verbs (remove る + られる) / Group 3 verbs (される / こられる)
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.why: In an emergency, the subject 'I' and the thief are omitted. The sentence focuses on the lost object and uses the passive form to report the loss.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: If the active form were used, the sentence would mean that the speaker had just stolen the wallet.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q5.kobun.tip: Learners often mistakenly use the active form ぬすみました, which changes the meaning to stealing something themselves.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vi: Although I hated exercise, my father often made me play sports.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は states the topic of the first clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle が goes with the adjective きらい to show the object of dislike.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The conjunction のに connects two contrasting clauses and adds feelings of dissatisfaction or regret.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle は states the person who performs the causative action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: This frequency adverb modifies the causative verb in the predicate.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に marks the person affected who must perform the causative action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle を marks the direct object of playing sports.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: The verb する changes to the causative form させる in the past tense to show that the father forced me to do it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.cn: Aな + なのに / Group 3 verbs: する → させる
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.why: The first clause uses のに to show a contrast with the speaker's personal wishes. The second clause uses the causative pattern 'N(person) に N(thing) を させる' to express being forced by someone else to perform an action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows that the father played sports for my benefit, which is completely different from being forced.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q6.kobun.tip: In a causative sentence with a transitive verb (which already has を), the person being made to act must take the particle に, not を.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vi: I got caught in the rain on my way home. And I had not even brought an umbrella...
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: A noun that indicates a time, used with the particle に to modify the time when an event occurs.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に marks a natural event that causes trouble in the indirect passive.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.2.vi: fell on me and got me wet.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The intransitive verb 降る changes to the passive form 降られる to describe the speaker's trouble from being caught in the rain.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle を marks an object that the person did not have with them.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.4.vi: had not brought it, even though....
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The structure のに appears at the end of the sentence with an ellipsis to express deep regret and dissatisfaction.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.cn: Group 1 verbs (a-row + れる) / V普通形 + のに
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.why: The first sentence uses the passive of an intransitive verb 雨に降られる to describe the trouble caused by being caught in the rain. The second sentence trails off with のに to emphasize regret and annoyance about not having an umbrella.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: It only objectively states that it rained, without showing that the speaker had trouble or got wet.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q8.kobun.vi: Because my daughter wanted to attend university, I let her go.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the subject of the subordinate clause stating the reason.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle へ marks the direction and destination of the study-related action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The ending たがる expresses a third person's wish, combined with the conjunction ので, which gives an objective reason.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 行く changes to the causative form 行かせる in the past tense, with the meaning of giving permission according to someone's wish.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vi: A: 'Could you listen to my story a little longer?' - B: 'Sorry, I do not have time today.'

default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object received through the action of listening.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb of amount and degree that modifies the act of listening.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The polite request pattern Vてくださいませんか ends A's suggestion.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle は states the time reference as the topic of the sentence.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: It is an imperative and a direct request, so it is less polite and gentle than くださいませんか.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t6-q9.kobun.tip: The pattern 〜てくださいませんか is a very polite way to make a request. It asks whether the other person can do something for you; it is not a negative question.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: It identifies the speaker of the dialogue.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q1.kobun.cn: Group 1 verbs: change the u-ending to e (命令形). V辞書形 + な (禁止形).

default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q1.kobun.tip: Do not confuse the prohibitive form (dictionary-form V + な), which forbids an action, with the particle な at the end of a sentence, which expresses emotion or confirms information.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vi: There is a parked car in front of my house. Someone is sleeping inside it.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に identifies the place where the car is parked.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject that is parked in front of the house.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The intransitive verb combined with ている expresses the continuing result of the act of parking.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle で identifies the place where the action of sleeping takes place.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.5.n: An interrogative word combined with the particle か forms an indefinite pronoun referring to a person of unknown identity.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.ch.6.n: The verb combined with ている expresses an action in progress at the time of speaking.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.why: The first sentence uses the intransitive verb (とまる) combined with ている to describe the resulting state of the car. The second sentence uses an action verb (ねる) combined with ている to describe a person's ongoing sleep.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Use the transitive verb とめる combined with てある to emphasize that someone deliberately parked the car there.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It describes the moment when someone has just started to fall asleep, rather than emphasizing a continuous state of sleep.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q2.kobun.tip: It is necessary to distinguish Vている of an intransitive verb, which indicates the resulting state after an event, from Vている of an action verb, which indicates an ongoing process.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vi:

default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: Names the speaker in the second turn.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: A time adverb referring to the past and marking when an event happened.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle に marks the person who caused the forced action in the passive causative sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: An adverb of degree modifying the amount of alcohol that the speaker was forced to drink.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of drinking.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.8.n: The verb in the passive causative form combines with the ending んです to explain the hardship the speaker experienced.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.9.n: A conjunction showing a cause-and-effect relationship leading to the unpleasant condition.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.10.n: The particle も emphasizes that the unpleasant condition has continued until the present.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.11.n: The particle が accompanies a noun describing a bodily condition and makes it the subject of the adjective わるい.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.ch.12.n: The adjective ending い combines with the ending んです to clearly explain the speaker's current tired condition.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.cn: Group 1 verbs: change the final u sound to asareru. Group 2 verbs: change the final ru to saserareru. Group 3 verbs: suru changes to saserareru, and kuru changes to koserareru.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.why: Tanaka uses the passive causative form (飲まされた) to describe being unwillingly forced to drink alcohol, then uses the ending んです to explain the cause of his current unpleasant condition.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses gratitude for being invited or allowed by the other person to drink alcohol, which is completely opposite to the meaning of being forced.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: The ordinary passive form means that someone drank the speaker's alcohol, not that the speaker was forced to drink.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q3.kobun.tip: Group 1 verbs often have the shortened ending -asareru, such as 飲まされた, but verbs ending in す, such as 話す, must be changed to -saserareta (話させられた).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vi: The doctor told me to sleep more.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle に identifies the person giving advice or instructions in the passive sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: An adverb of degree modifying the action of sleeping.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern ように is used to indirectly quote the content of advice or a request.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb 言う in the passive form shows that the speaker received a reminder from the doctor.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.why: The indirect quotation structure Vように言われた is used to gently and politely report the doctor's advice or instructions to the speaker.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: A direct quotation of the imperative form と言われた, which sounds rougher and stronger than ように言われた.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.vs.1.d: The active form means that the speaker told another person to sleep more, rather than receiving the advice.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.tip: When quoting a prohibition or reminder not to do something, change the verb to the negative form Vない + ように, for example: 無理をしないように言われた.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q4.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + ように言われる・頼まれる・注意される
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vi: According to the news, this summer will be hot, you know.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The grammar pattern によると clearly states the information source for the statement that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: A time noun combined with the particle の modifies the noun “summer.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は identifies summer as the main topic.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: A verb phrase expressing a change in the state of the weather.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.4.vi: I hear that it will, you know.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The grammar pattern そうだ expresses reported information and combines with the modal particle よ.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.cn: N + によると + plain-form clause (普通形) + そうだ
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.why: The pattern によると is placed at the beginning of the sentence to state the information source, current news, and is combined with そうだ at the end to report the weather forecast objectively.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses the speaker's judgment or expectation based on visible signs, such as the impression that it is about to become hot, rather than reported information.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: It expresses an inference based on information heard from others, but the source is less clearly official than そうだ.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q5.kobun.tip: Distinguish the reported-information form そうだ, which follows the plain form (あつくなるそうだ), from the visual-judgment form そうだ, which drops the adjective or verb ending (あつそうだ).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vi: I hear that Tokyo is a scary place. So do not let your daughter go there.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は identifies Tokyo as the main topic being judged.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in い directly modifies the following noun for a place.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: A noun combined with the predicate particle だ forms the predicate before the reported-information pattern.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The grammar pattern そうだ expresses information heard from another person.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: A conjunction showing a cause-and-effect relationship and introducing the prohibition in the following clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle を marks the person affected by the causative action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: The causative verb form 行かせる combines with the particle な to form a prohibition meaning “do not allow her to go.”
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうだ (reported information). V(使役形・辞書形) + な (prohibition).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.why: The first sentence reports information heard about Tokyo, using Nだそうだ, as the basis for the firm prohibition in the second sentence: do not let the listener's daughter go (the causative form 行かせる combined with the particle な).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: A polite request or warning not to let her go, without the harsh command-like tone of 行かせるな.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: A direct prohibition telling the listener not to go, whereas 行かせるな prohibits the listener from letting a third person, the daughter, go.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q6.kobun.tip: The structure V使役形 + な means prohibiting someone from allowing another person to perform an action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.vi: It seems my daughter will be in your care. Thank you very much.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.sk: N が + お世話になる + Vます語幹 + そうで + expression of thanks
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle が marks the person who is expected to receive care.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: お世話になる means being cared for or helped by someone else; ～そうで connects this prediction to the thanks that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: ありがとうございました is a polite expression of thanks for help received or about to be received.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.cn: Vます形の語幹・Aい語幹・Aな語幹 + そうだ; そうだ → そうで when joining clauses
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.why: 娘が is the subject of お世話になる, not the person directly providing the help. ～そうで expresses a prediction based on the situation and then connects naturally to the thanks.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If the information-reporting meaning were used, the sentence would mean that it is said that my daughter will be helped, rather than being the speaker's own prediction.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If replaced with ～ようで, the prediction would sound more formal and more like a judgment based on signs.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may understand お世話になる as personally taking care of someone, but this pattern usually means being cared for or helped by someone else.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: The noun predicate combines with ですね to seek agreement from the listener.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.2.vi: I really want to eat it!
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb takes the たい form to express the speaker's direct desire.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.cn: V(remove ます)・Aい(remove い)・Aな + そうだ / そうな + N
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.why: The visual-prediction pattern そうだ follows the adjective おいしい after removing い, and changes to そうな when it comes before the noun ケーキ to modify it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: It states that the cake is delicious as a known fact or based on having tasted it, not as a prediction from its appearance.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: This is grammatically incorrect because keeping い gives a reported-information meaning and it cannot change into the form そうな N.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q8.kobun.tip: When using そうだ to describe appearance (looks...), remove the ending い of an adjective ending in い before combining them.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vi: According to Mr. Yamada, I hear that the movie theater is not very far away.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: It modifies the noun 話 to identify the person providing the information.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The structure Nによると states the source of the reported information.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle は makes the location, the movie theater, the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: An adverb of degree used with a negative predicate.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The negative form of the adjective とおい serves as the predicate of the information clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.5.vi: I hear that it is..., you know.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The pattern そうだ reports information and combines with the particle よ to tell the listener something they do not yet know.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.why: The phrase ～によると at the beginning states the information source and must be combined with the reporting pattern ～そうだ at the end to repeat what was heard.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses a prediction based on rumors or an indirect impression, with more emphasis on guessing than on directly quoting information.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: It describes the speaker's direct impression ('it looks not far'), so it is not suitable when a clear source has already been given.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.tip: When Nによると (according to...) appears at the beginning, the sentence must end with a reporting structure such as そうだ, not with an ordinary statement.
