default.q.speedvp_n4-t7-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aなだ・Nだ + そうだ
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vi: If I were a bird, I would fly back to my country right away.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.sk: もし + N だったら + Vて + N へ + V(remove ます)たい
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb showing a supposition, often used with the conditional structure たら.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: A noun combines with だったら to present an unreal hypothetical condition.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb takes the て form to connect the way the action is carried out before returning.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle へ shows the direction and destination of the action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.ch.4.n: The predicate expresses the speaker's personal wish using the たい form.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.why: The adverb もし combines with the hypothetical form だったら to create an unreal assumption in the first clause, leading to the wish 帰りたい in the second clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: It is often used to give advice or respond to a topic just mentioned by someone else. It is less natural than たら for an unreal supposition.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.vs.1.d: It shows an inevitable result or natural development, so the following clause cannot express intention or a wish (たい).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.tip: The conditional pattern と cannot be used with a following clause expressing intention or desire (たい, つもり), while たら can be used freely.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q1.kobun.cn: Vた・Aいかった・Aなだった・Nだった + ら
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vi: If you are going to be absent from school or work, you must contact us.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.sk: V辞書形 + 場合は + かならず + V(ない form, remove い) + ければならない
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the noun 場合は to describe the situation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: A formal noun combines with は to make the condition the topic.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: An adverb that emphasizes the necessity or obligation of the action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The predicate uses the structure なければならない to express a rule or obligation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.why: The structure 場合は establishes a formal, rule-based condition. It combines with the adverb かならず and the obligation ending なければならない to clearly state the rule that must be followed.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: It sounds more casual and refers to a general time, rather than a specific situation or rule like 場合は.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.vs.1.d: It implies accepting the other person's intention and then giving an immediate response or request.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.tip: Before 場合は, a noun must be connected with the particle の (Nの場合), and an adjective ending in な must keep な (Aな場合); do not use だ.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q2.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nの + 場合(は)
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vi: Today I plan not to go to school but to stay home and rest.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は follows a time word to establish the sentence topic.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に shows the destination of the movement.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The pattern Vないで means not doing this action but doing another action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle で shows the place where the resting action takes place.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The plain-form verb directly modifies the noun つもり.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: A sentence-ending pattern showing a personal intention or plan that has already been decided.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.why: The pattern V1ないで V2 expresses the choice not to do V1 (go to school) but to do V2 (stay home and rest), combined with つもりです at the end to express the speaker's plan.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: It shows a cause or reason ('because I will not go...'), not the choice of replacing one action with another as in 行かないで.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: It only expresses a negative plan ('plan not to go') and cannot create a sequence in which a later action replaces the first one.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.tip: Do not confuse Vないで (not doing A but doing B—a choice) with Vなくて (only a cause and result).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q3.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vない形 + つもりだ
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vi: According to the weather forecast, I hear that it will be hot tomorrow.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: The noun phrase combines with 「によると」 to state the information source for the report at the end of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle 「は」 makes "tomorrow" the main topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.2.vi: I hear that it will be hot.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The adjective ending in い keeps its ordinary form and combines with 「そうです」 to report heard information.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.why: The phrase 「〜によると」 is placed at the beginning to confirm the reliable information source and provide the basis for the reporting pattern 「〜そうです」 at the end of the predicate.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: It expresses an intuitive judgment from appearance ('it looks hot') instead of reporting information from another source.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.tip: Clearly distinguish the reporting form 「Aい + そうです」 (I hear that it is hot, keeping い) from the prediction form 「A without い + そうです」 (it looks hot).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q4.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい普通形・Aなだ・Nだ ＋ そうだ／そうです（伝聞）
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.vi: Because of the snow, it is said that many car accidents are happening.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The phrase 「N ＋ のため」 states an objective cause leading to the result described in the following clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle 「の」 modifies the noun 「事故」 to clarify that this is a car accident.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle 「が」 marks the subject used with the intransitive verb 「起きる」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: This adverb modifies the degree of the verb 「起きている」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The verb in the progressive form combines with 「そうです」 to express that the event is reportedly continuing in many places.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.why: The first clause uses 「N ＋ のため」 to state an objective reason in a formal tone, while the second clause uses 「〜ているそうです」 to report an ongoing phenomenon based on received information.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: This is more conversational and expresses a more subjective reason than the objective, formal nuance of 「雪のため」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.tip: When 「ため」 is used with a noun, the particle 「の」 must be added (N のため); do not attach it directly to N ため.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q5.kobun.cn: Nの・V普通形・Aい・Aな ＋ ため（に）
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vi: When I went to my girlfriend's house for the first time, I greeted her father at the entrance.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: It modifies the noun 「家」 to identify ownership or the place where someone lives.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle 「に」 indicates the destination of the movement action 「行く」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.2.vi: when I went there for the first time,
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The time clause uses 「Vた ＋ とき」 to show that the following action happened only after arriving completely.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle 「で」 indicates the specific place where the greeting took place.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.4.n: It modifies the noun 「お父さん」 to clarify the family member involved.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle 「に」 indicates the person who receives the greeting.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle 「を」 marks the direct object used with the verb 「した」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.ch.7.n: The main predicate ends in the past tense to report a completed event.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.why: The past form 「行ったとき」 is used because the movement to the house was complete—the speaker had already reached the entrance—before the greeting took place.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: This indicates the time before leaving or while traveling to the house, so it does not fit because the greeting happened after arriving at the entrance.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.tip: Remember that if the action in the following clause happens AFTER the action of going or arriving is complete, before 「とき」 the verb must be changed to the past form 「Vた」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q6.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形・Aい・Aな・Nの ＋ とき（に）
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vi: Yesterday, when I went to her house, I bought a gift and took it with me.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.sk: Time ＋ N の ＋ N に ＋ Vた形 ＋ とき ＋ N を ＋ Vて ＋ Vた
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: This phrase states the time when the whole event took place.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: の connects かのじょ with 家, creating a noun phrase meaning the house that belongs to her.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle に marks the destination of 行く.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: Vた形 ＋ とき forms a time clause that provides the setting for buying the gift.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle を marks the thing that was bought.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.5.n: 買って connects with 行った and shows that the buying happened before taking it away.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.ch.6.n: 行った completes the sequence of actions and, in 買って行った, carries the nuance of buying something and taking it to another place.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.why: きのう states the general time, while かのじょの家に行ったとき creates the time point for the following action. 買って行った uses the て form to connect the two actions in the order of buying and then taking the gift away.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If とき is replaced with ～たあとで, the meaning emphasizes that the buying happened after going there, rather than while arriving there.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.vs.1.d: If ～てから is used, the sentence emphasizes more clearly that going happened first and buying happened afterward.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily translate 買って行った as “buy and go,” but 行く after the て form usually emphasizes carrying or taking an object away.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q7.kobun.cn: V普通形 ＋ とき; Aい ＋ とき; Aな ＋ なとき; N ＋ のとき
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vi: When you leave, I will give you the cake I baked today, so remember to take it home.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: The structure 「V辞書形 ＋ ときに」 identifies the time when someone is about to leave, preparing for the action of giving the cake.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: This time adverb modifies the action of baking the cake 「焼いた」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: The past-tense verb acts as a relative clause that directly modifies 「ケーキ」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle 「を」 marks the direct object being given.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.4.vi: because I will give it to you,
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The connecting particle 「から」 gives the reason for the reminder in the following clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: The 「〜て」 verb form with the sentence-ending particle 「ね」 creates a friendly request between friends.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.why: 「帰るときに」 (the dictionary form) is used because the cake will be given when the person is preparing to leave, before they have fully gone; 「から」 connects the explanatory clause to the reminder 「持って帰ってね」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: This indicates after the other person has already returned fully to their home, when the speaker can no longer hand over the cake directly.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.tip: Do not use 「帰ったときに」 in the context of giving something before saying goodbye, because the 「Vた」 form shows that the person has already arrived home.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q8.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形・Aい・Aな・Nの ＋ とき（に）
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q9.kobun.vi: Whenever I manage to cook something delicious, I naturally want someone to enjoy eating it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle 「を」 marks the object of the potential verb 「つくれた」.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The adjective ending in い changes to the 「〜く」 form to modify the following verb.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.2.vi: when I manage to cook it,
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The past potential verb form 「Vた ＋ とき」 expresses the situation or time after successfully cooking the food.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle 「に」 follows an interrogative word and indicates the person whom the speaker wants to perform the action for them.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.4.vi: want someone to eat it for me.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The predicate phrase combines 「〜てもらう」 (receiving an action) + 「〜たい」 (desire) + 「〜くなる」 (a natural feeling arising).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q9.kobun.why: 「つくれたとき」 (the past potential form) sets the context after the food has been cooked successfully and tastes good; only then does the desire to share it arise.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: This indicates a time while cooking is still in progress, before the food is finished, so it does not fit the feeling of immediately inviting someone to eat.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q9.kobun.tip: Note that the pattern 「〜てもらう」 goes with the particle 「に」 (だれかに) to indicate the person who performs an action that benefits the speaker.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t8-q9.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Vた形・Aい・Aな・Nの ＋ とき（に）
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.vi: I am saving money to get married.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.0.n: The subordinate clause used with the pattern ために expresses the subject’s intentional purpose.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle を marks the object affected by the action of saving.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.ch.2.n: The verb form ています expresses an action that continues over time.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.why: The purpose clause comes first and modifies the act of saving money in the following clause. Getting married is the intentional goal.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.vs.0.d: Use this when the first clause contains a non-volitional verb or a potential form to indicate a desired state.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.tip: The verb before ために must express intention, and the subjects of both clauses must be the same person.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q1.kobun.cn: V辞書形・Nの ＋ ために
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.vi: I want to raise this child in a way that reflects a child’s natural innocence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.0.n: The demonstrative before it limits and modifies the noun 子.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle は makes the child the topic of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.2.n: The suffix らしい changes to the adverbial form らしく to modify the following verb for raising a child.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.ch.3.n: The verb ending たい combines with です to express the speaker’s polite desire.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.why: The pattern らしい shows that the action matches the object’s natural character (the child acts like a child). It changes to the adverbial form らしく to modify the verb そだてたい directly.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.vs.0.d: Use this to make a figurative comparison with something else, although the object is not actually that thing.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.tip: Do not confuse らしい, which shows the object’s true nature, with ようだ, which figuratively compares an object with something it is not.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q2.kobun.cn: N ＋ らしく ＋ V / N ＋ らしい ＋ N

default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle も lists the first factor in the series of changes.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle し lists an objective event as a reason.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle も continues the list with a second factor of the same type.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.5.n: The particle し ends the list of reasons and clarifies the statement in the previous sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.6.n: The interjection shows agreement with A’s comment.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.7.n: An adverb marking the point in time when change begins to move toward the future.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.8.n: An adverb of degree modifying the change.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.ch.9.n: The pattern ていく expresses continuing change toward the future, combined with でしょう for a gentle guess.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: Indicates change from the past to the present or movement toward the speaker.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q3.kobun.tip: Clearly distinguish ていく, which indicates movement away or continuation toward the future, from てくる, which indicates movement closer or change from the past to the present.

default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.vi: I ate too much, so my stomach started to hurt. Therefore, I would like to take the day off.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.0.n: An adverb of quantity modifying the act of eating in the following clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.1.n: The form たら describes a sequence of actions that leads to a discovery or an unwanted result.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle が marks the subject of the state that arises.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.3.n: The adjective ending い changes to く and combines with なりました to indicate a natural change of state.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.4.n: A conjunction showing a cause-and-effect relationship leading to the request to take the day off.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.5.vi: I will take the day off.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.ch.5.n: The main predicate expresses the speaker’s decision to act.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.why: The first clause uses the structure たら to connect eating with the change of state of having a stomachache (いたくなる). It then uses the conjunction だから to connect the cause with the decision to take the day off in the next sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.vs.0.d: Indicates the intentional action of a person causing a change of state, unlike なる, which indicates a natural change.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.tip: When an adjective ending in い combines with なる, remove い and change it to く (do not use いたいになる).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q4.kobun.cn: Aいく・Aなに・Nに ＋ なる
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.vi: There seems to be someone in the next room. I can hear a woman talking.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle の connects the location modifier to the noun for room.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle に indicates the place where the subject exists.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.2.n: An indefinite pronoun referring to someone whose identity is not known.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.3.n: The ending らしい is used to make a guess based on the actual sound in the next sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.4.n: The subject performing the action of speaking in the relative clause.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.5.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the noun 声 immediately after it.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle が combines with the perception verb 聞こえる to indicate the sound being perceived.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.ch.7.n: An intransitive verb indicating that a sound naturally reaches the speaker’s ears.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.why: The speaker hears a woman’s voice (聲が聞こえる) as direct, objective evidence, and uses らしい to guess that someone is present.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.vs.0.d: Used to report information heard from someone else, rather than making a personal guess from a directly heard sound.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.vs.1.d: Expresses a subjective guess based on the speaker’s intuition or impression.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.tip: The pattern らしい connects directly to nouns and adjectives ending in な, without adding だ or な.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q5.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな語幹・N ＋ らしい
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.vi: Although that child is already 10 years old, their actions are just like those of a newborn baby.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.0.n: The particle は marks the subject being commented on or evaluated.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.1.n: The pattern なのに expresses a contrast with the usual expectation for that age.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.2.n: The noun combines with the particle の to connect to the following comparison structure.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.ch.3.n: The comparison pattern ようだ presents an image comparing one object with another.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.why: The first clause gives the contrasting fact using なのに (already 10 years old). The second clause uses N のようだ to compare the child’s character or behavior to that of a newborn baby.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.vs.0.d: Indicates a quality that matches the true nature of something (if the object is really a baby and behaves like a baby).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.vs.1.d: Used to directly judge appearance through sight (what something seems to look like).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.tip: When ようだ is used to compare with a noun, the particle の must come between them (Nのようだ).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q6.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな・Nの + ようだ / ようです
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.vi: Today's test was not as difficult as last week's test.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.0.n: The time phrase directly modifies the noun "テスト" that follows.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.1.n: The particle "は" makes today's test the topic of comparison.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.2.n: The time noun phrase modifies the noun "テスト".
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.3.n: The particle "ほど" is used with a negative predicate to show that something is not as much as the comparison standard.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.ch.4.n: The past negative form of the い-ending adjective serves as the main predicate of the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.why: The structure 'N1 は N2 ほど + negative adjective/verb' is used for an inferior comparison. It shows that N1 does not reach the level of N2.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.vs.0.d: If 'より' is used, the sentence must be affirmative to make a comparative statement (e.g., 先週のテストよりむずかしかった).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.tip: Do not use 'ほど' in an affirmative sentence when expressing equality. The structure 'ほど...ない' must always be used with a negative ending.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q7.kobun.cn: N + ほど + Aい否定・Aな否定・V否定
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.vi: Child: "Mom, please wash the clothes I will wear next week in advance." Mother: "Wash them yourself."
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.0.n: Identifies the speaker in the first turn.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.1.n: Calling for the mother’s attention before making a request.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.2.n: A time adverb modifying the action of wearing the clothes.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.3.n: The dictionary-form verb modifies the noun "服" to form the phrase 'clothes to wear'.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle "を" marks the object affected by the washing action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.5.n: The verb is changed to the "〜ておく" form and then used in the informal spoken form "〜ておいて" to ask someone to prepare something in advance.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.6.n: Identifies the speaker in the reply.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.7.n: The particle "で" indicates the method and shows that the subject performs the action alone.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.ch.8.n: The pattern "〜なさい" is used by parents or other higher-status people to order or ask someone of lower status to perform an action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.why: The child uses '〜ておいて' to ask the mother to prepare something in advance for next week, while the mother uses '〜なさい' to give a reminder-like command to the child.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 'あらってみて', the sentence means 'try washing it' rather than preparing it in advance.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.vs.1.d: If the mother uses 'あらいなさい', it sounds more superior and commanding than the polite request 'あらってください'.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.tip: The pattern '〜なさい' is used only by a higher-status person speaking to someone of lower status, such as a parent to a child or a teacher to a student. It must never be used with a higher-status person.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q8.kobun.cn: Vて + おく / おいて ｜ Vます形 + なさい
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vi: A: "Do you know Shun's phone number?" B: "I don't know, but Hana might know."
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: Identifies A as the person asking.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: The possessive noun phrase modifies "電話番号".
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The particle "を" identifies the information that needs to be known.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: The progressive-form verb is used in an informal question about the state of knowing some information.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: The particle "は" states the subject and also adds a tone of explanation and contrast.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.5.n: The negative verb form combines with "けど" to create a gentle contrasting clause in conversation.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.6.n: The particle "なら" presents Hana as a suitable hypothetical topic.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.ch.7.n: The pattern "〜かもしれない" expresses the speaker's uncertain guess, with about 50% certainty.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.why: After the contrasting clause '〜けど', the speaker uses 'なら' to introduce someone who may know. The cautious judgment ending '〜かもしれない' is used because the speaker is not completely certain.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced with 'わかるはずだ', it shows a very high level of certainty based on a clear reason or basis (she is certain to know).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If 'わかるでしょう' is used, it shows a more certain judgment than 'かもしれない'.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.tip: When used with a noun or an な-ending adjective, 'かもしれない' connects directly without adding 'だ' or 'な' (e.g., はなさんかもしれない, not はなさんだかもしれない).
default.q.speedvp_n4-t9-q9.kobun.cn: V普通形・Aい・Aな（語幹）・N + かもしれない
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vi: I am about to eat. Would you like to eat with me?
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.0.n: これから indicates the time when an action is about to begin.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.1.n: を marks ごはん as the object of 食べる.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.2.n: The dictionary-form verb 食べる comes before ところです to express an action that is about to begin.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.3.n: に indicates the manner or the person performing the action together with someone else.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.ch.4.n: どうですか is used to ask for the listener's opinion and suggest joining the action.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.why: これから states the time, ごはんを marks the object, and 食べるところです shows that eating has not started but will begin soon. Then, いっしょに どうですか creates an invitation to do the action together.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes that the person is eating at the moment of speaking, not about to eat.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the meaning becomes that the person has just finished eating.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily use 食べているところです to say that they are about to eat, but this pattern actually describes an action in progress.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t1-q9.kobun.cn: V辞書形 + ところです
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.vi: It has recently become a little cooler, so I am very happy.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.0.n: さいきん modifies the entire change and emotion in the sentence.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.1.n: 少し modifies the degree of becoming cooler.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.2.n: The い-ending adjective changes into the く form to connect with なる and create the meaning 'become cooler'.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.ch.3.n: なってきて connects the change with うれしい and shows that the change started earlier and has progressed to the present.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.why: すずしく is in the く form to combine with なる and create a structure expressing a change of state. てくる shows a change that started in the past and is moving toward the present. It then connects with うれしい to state the speaker's emotion.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.vs.0.d: If it is replaced, the sentence emphasizes that the current state is cool, rather than the process of changing toward the present.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.vs.1.d: If it is replaced, the sentence describes a change that continues toward the future.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.tip: Vietnamese learners may easily connect すずしい directly with なる, but it must be changed to すずしくなる because an い-ending adjective needs the く form before なる.
default.q.speedvp_n4-t17-q3.kobun.cn: Aいく + なる + てくる・Aなに + なる + てくる・Nに + なる + てくる
